TL;DR: The game is amazing from a design/story point of view, negatively impacted from bad controls and challenging but not as hard as people say after rage quiting the first boss or two.
Lots of reviews out there either absolutely love or hate the Souls series and I would say the differentiating factor is breaking through the wall of really getting into the game. The game is all about feelings of accomplishment while being challenging enough to make the accomplishment seem meaningful. The challenges are also far more fair than most people expect because most enemies follow the same rules you are constrained with during combat.
The ever present "get good" advice does apply but the game is all about perservering to the point it is an intended story element in the game. The game is definitely impacted by rather clunky controls and sometimes bad collision detection but you shouldn't be playing this game because of the elegent fighting system. This game is probably one of my favorites because of all the careful design decisions that went into what seems like almost every aspect of the game.
I would recommend this game to any "serious" gamer who enjoys a challenge. However, if you don't care about game design, lore or story then I would have a harder time recommending the game because all that is left is the feelings of accomplishment. I have played through this game more times than any other game for a reason and still seem to find new things about it I didn't know the previous time through. If you're having trouble getting into it, look up lore explanation videos to get you to be more invested in the world and understand why I'd call it a work of art.

I have to run this game off my laptop in order for it to recognize the controller. I won't recommend this game on pc. DSfix doesn't fix the controller issues. You essentially have to unplug and disable all usb devices for it to recognize a controller. If you're going to play this game, that's all you will be doing with your computer. This game has incredible level design. I can see why it's considered a classic, so it is worth trying on another system, or if you absolutely know it will work on your pc with a controller. There are however issues that are swept under the rug by the community that when brought up cause a cult like attack on forums. The two biggest issues in this game when it works on pc are the camera and the hit boxes. Both are incredibly finicky and difficult to predict or understand. This leads to bosses cornering and stun locking you, enemies attacking through walls when your weapons can't, massive bosses in tight spaces causing the camera to spin if you lock on. This accounts for a lot of my frustration. When those things work this game is incredibly satisfying. It's like a fantasy tactical shooter. You have to check corners and memorize layouts, use shortcuts to get the jump on enemies. It's so close to being an incredible fantasy rpg, but these issues crop up a lot and really dampen the experience. The real shame is that the community jumps on anyone who criticizes these issues and so they remain prevalent in the future games too. When the combat is difficult but fair, the combat system is some of the best the fantasy rpg genre has to offer, but too often technical issues crop up and lead to unavoidable deaths. Git Gud does nothing to fix these issues or grow and improve the franchise.
I'm an avid player of the monster hunter series and the witcher as well. Those two games have the best melee combat design in fantasy rpgs. They require commitment to your swings and strategic positioning. I thought dark souls was heading in that direction but after fighting the silver knights and giant guardians in anor londo I found what makes the combat system so difficult. The rules for combat change from enemy to enemy and move to move. Sword silver knights swing leaving themselves open to attack, but the giants and spearmen passively block with their shield. It's a complete guess as to whether enemies are open to attack or not. Also enemies will spam attacks. Couple that with a broken camera, changing rules, uneven hitboxes and loads of clipping problems and you get a difficult game, yes. Strategic and fair, absolutely not. There is no strategy to this game. Good positioning still gets you hit by the tail end of the spear while it thrusts away from you. Either you perfect the parry and backstab and deal with every enemy that way, or take a gamble on enemy moves and the rules that will apply to the one they are winding up for. Enemy size doesn't matter, they can turn on a dime and skate around 180 degrees mid attack to hit you. Made it around their back successfully, too bad, you still take damage. Enemies can block and attack at the same time as well as queue up new attacks immediately after finishing old ones. The player has their inputs queued up as well so you can press attack, but if the boss hits you first you will get hit again and again only to stand up 10 seconds later and swing, depleting your stamina bar allowing you to be stun locked again. In monster hunter the combat is like a dance. You read the enemy wind up and then respond. It has slow animations, but the rules remain the same for every monster and every player. In the witcher you aggro enemies into moves and then dodge and attack or parry, predicting their next move. The combat system in this game is close but there are so many minor oversights that break the combat flow. The rules are so inconsistent and the risk reward system allows for losing hours of progress when you weren't taking very big risks. That is why this game is frustrating and I don't think it needs that to be as challenging or rewarding as it claims to be. Add to this a huge drop in level design quality towards the later game and it just becomes a boring slog. I'm at the point where I don't feel like I'm learning anything when I die, I'm just backtracking and farming the same enemies over and over again until one of these problems crops up, then I get to do it all over again. I guess I've lost the motivation to play this anymore. The reward of progression and satisfaction of overcoming increasingly difficult enemies is gone. It's just a slog now, and every death feels like a waste of my time. It's really rewarding discovering the map and shortcuts but aside from that I can't find a reason to recommend this game. I like it because I've played for forty hours, but it's not the greatest game of the past decade, and the pc version is certainly not worth $20 for all the work you have to put in just to get the game to function.

From year 2003, the third instalment of the series,
makes a radical change of presentation by carrying our beloved protagonists to 3D! Yup, it's the start of the millennium and 3D adventure games are big at the time. Knights Templar, Slavic assassins, medieval conspiracies and much more for us to enjoy in 3D this time. Expectedly, this change comes with a whole new set of game mechanics too. Not to worry though! The setting, the environment and the tone of the game are trademark George & Nico quality, alright!
Following the events of the previous game, George goes back to his life as a patent lawyer and finds himself flying to the Congo to meet a scientist who claims that his machine can produce limitless energy. However, the plane crashes during a storm and George barely saves his hide. He takes a walk to meet the scientist, and yet again, finds himself in a conspiracy involving - wait for it - Templars! Meanwhile, Nico, still working for her paper, is called to interview a hacker who claims that he cracked Voynich manuscript and warns hectically about an "end of the world" scenario. Going to meet the guy, Nico finds him dead - of course - and gets attacked by the assassin who was impersonating her! As sure as the careful hands of fate would deem so, they again get together to solve the mystery, save the world and beat some Templar♥♥♥♥♥while doing so.
In this adventure to come, we will meet new faces and encounter some familiar ones from previous games, going on another adventure that would rally us around the globe. That's one thing that I love about Broken Sword games. You get to visit countless different locations with different cultures and get introduced to anecdotes from their local lore. Yet, somehow, all those seemingly irrelevant details come together to paint a bigger picture. Its Indiana Jones meets Dan Brown every time. Humor is spot on also, this time relying on both folklore narrative and sexual innuendo a bit more than usual. One other thing is that we are capable of observing George and Nico's relationship growth based on their mutual history, growing inner jokes and references to previous games. Both George and Nico are just as you remember them: a lovable, smart♥♥♥♥♥Yankee with a law degree and an ambitious, pretty reporter with a sharp tongue.
Let's get to the obvious change then, shall we? Our good old 2D P&C environment is no more. Now we have 3D cartoon renderings of our beloved characters and there is no "clicking" on the literal sense. Yup, mouse is pretty much useless in this instalment. All interactions are controlled from the keyboard, including item selection and movement - which is kinda okay. What would be a real drag is cameras. They change into pretty obscure point of views without warning, and it can become hellishly nasty if you are on a chasing scene. Oh, yes, we are also introduced with QTEs - quick time events - in this game. There will come some cinematic sequences in which you'll be asked to respond in a timely fashion by hitting the right button. Cute, huh? There aren't as many puzzles compared to previous games though, but the ones that we encounter are satisfying enough. Another newly introduced element is Sokoban games - a.k.a. box pushing puzzles. The game is riddled with them. They all are pretty easy, but mostly time consuming. You won't miss them when you finish the game.
All things aside,
is a neat little adventure game, even though it is slightly subpar in means of mechanics and brain scratching compared to previous titles. Its worthy of an experience for the jokes, the story and character interactions to begin with. Go ahead, play the game. You know you want to. It's George and Nico, and they are at another incredible adventure. It cannot be bad anyhow.

Ace Combat Assault Horizon - Enhanced Edition is both a fun and entertaining addition to the Ace Combat series.  It is an arcade, nervous, pick and play, flight combat game that I really enjoyed playing.  It is clear that the game makers were trying to mirror the Call of Duty's campaign mode strengths.  In other words, the campaign is explosive, very intense, nervous, and chaotic at moments, as if you are part of a Michael Bay movie.   I personally found it very refreshing and I hope that future sequels will keep this vision.  Finally keep in mind that this is not a hardcore/realistic flight simulator.  Below are my pros and cons :
Positives:
*  Awesome campaign mode.
*  Easy gameplay (with depth at high levels)
*  Nervous  (dog)fights.
*  Great music and sounds (The japanese voices are outstanding.  The english ones are not so good/bad).
*  Pick and play (meaning you don't need to know who is who, or what is what, or what combination of buttons you need to press to make X or Y spell, or when you need to meet Z person at N's location, etc...  Just relax, pick your pad, get in this explosive universe, and enjoy yourself).
Negatives:
*  The scenario is a very "japanese" take on US politics/conflicts.
*  Short campaign (but very intense and fun).
Thanks to the developers for the enjoyable experience!
Verdict: A-

Based on Single Player gameplay...
WARNING!!! Frustration inducing game! lol  There are bosses that completely destroy your towers and continue to do so until they are killed!  One of them wiped out my best towers and then I lost the game the next round.  This was on the first map! Seems kind of unfair and unbalanced to present such bosses on the first map, but okay...  What is this? A rogue-like TD game! lmao
The game requires some trial and error to beat.  Tons of enemies just run right though my defenses every wave!  The developer changed the game because of complaints and it is now severely unbalanced and has some typos. There is no way to get a perfect endgame. Way too many creeps are released at once and your towers just cannot stop them all. Forget getting that perfect run satisfaction.
Advice: Build your strongest and best towers near the end of the map and make sure to use a lot of range/distance upgrades to win.  Those bosses can be rough!  Not sure about this game yet.  That boss encounter was almost a game breaker for me, because there is no way to repair towers.  You just watch as the boss lays waste to your towers! It's pretty frustrating!
Graphics are varied, but creeps are subpar, even at the highest settings. They work for a TD game.  Creeps are animated okay, but look like they are in slow motion.  It's weird. Sound was turned off as default. Once I turned on the sound, it was okay.  Sounds fit the game, but they are probably stock Unity sounds.  Nothing special.
Gamepad controls are turned on as default. You can choose keyboard & mouse in the settings, but the game is definitely optimized for gamepad use.  Mouse clicks are not always registered. My experience with my PS 4 wireless controller caused even more frustration, so I am using kb & mouse. There are a lot of different options in the menus to choose from, so that's a plus!
It was somewhat of a frustrating experience to watch my best towers get destroyed in seconds and no way to repair them.  Even if I could repair them, the boss destroyed them too quickly!  Certainly was unfair and a pure lesson in frustration! I did finally get past the first map after my second try but barely! lol I have since then beaten a few more maps, but it needs balancing IMO.
You can set targeting for towers which is standard for most TD games, but I have some TD that don't incorporate this feature and they suck for that. You can target nearest, fastest, strongest, etc... Makes a difference for sure!
Tower upgrades are handled two ways, so choose wisely! Some need cash (damage, range & rate of fire) and the more helpful upgrades use upgrade points, which you get after each mini-boss and boss encounter, but ONLY if you kill them! It would take too much time explaining everything here.  Just know that money and upgrade points are in short supply, so again, choose wisely.  Also, some towers seem severely underpowered, to the point of being useless.
Everything works great and I didn't experience any bugs or glitches.  I guess I'd ONLY recommend this to TD junkies that need a different experience in the TD genre and don't mind some trial and error gameplay... The developer is active and I'm sure he will iron things out in future patches. It's worth looking into on sale.

The bad:
What really gets to me though are the small, really simple issues, that soon a year after release really, REALLY should have been fixed. Like every map has 30 waves, when you complete them there is a "Congrats, you have cleared all
waves!"-message. It's a small and silly thing really, but since you get to see it after every map you start to sarcasticly roll with your eyes after a little while. There is this "continous mode" without any down time between waves. After all 30 waves have spawned the "completion fireworks" set off, even though you have yet to clear the last 4 waves.
And the game is riddled with those small things. Nothing game breaking mind you, yet enough to annoy. Move this button five pixels so the mouse scroll works in all directions? Guilty Gear Xrd is essentially a huge step up from other 2D fighters that were ported to the PC. It has little to no bugs especially with arcsys working hard to fix the game often. For a game not originally made with a PC port it's got pretty good online play albeit it still needs improvements.
Pros:
To start off with what GGXrd does right is that for a game that was originally for PS3/PS4, it runs just as, if not even better on PC. No real input delay, and is even supported by a diverse amount of controllers (keyboard included). Although it should be noted that the controller needs to be plugged in before you start the game otherwise the game will only recognize the keyboard inputs.
Graphicswise it looks and performs better than the PS3/PS4 version (as long as you have a graphics card better than the standard Intel card). However, the game can still even run around 50-60 fps on the Intel graphics if you turn down the settings. Don't expect it to look pretty though. The game itself runs on Unreal Engine 3 which was originally intended for Windows.
Also, the online lobby system is one of the best I've seen. It has 8 player lobbies, with 4 battle rooms for those players to interact. So it doesn't just come down to 8 players with 2 fighting while 6 spectate. You have full control of your player icon to move around the rooms and switch what battle room you want to participate in. Whether you want to play winner next in line or just spectate. There's even an AFK section for players who haven't pressed a button in awhile so people don't get stuck on empty battle rooms.
The character cast itself is really well done for a fighting game. Very diverse and stylish character designs. And the characters themselves offer playstyles suited for almost everyone. Starting from simple straightforward characters like Sol Badguy and Ky Kiske, to zoners like Axl, and for the people who like playing two characters at once there's Zato-1.
Cons:
This is not really a problem I've come across with the PS3/PS4 version. However, it's worth mentioning because people are bound to come across this issue. Like I mentioned previously, the online play itself works fine. Connecting into player lobbies is mostly consistent especially if you're playing with someone in the same region. Playing with someone far away can cause input delay, which can even reach to 10-14 frame delay which is almost unplayable. In my experience, I've tried playing with people on the other side of the world and sometimes had 4 ms delay so it can work sometimes far away. The biggest problem with GGXrd on the PC port is that there's problems connecting to people, especially with ranked mode. And also if you're playing on strict NAT you won't be able to connect to people at all. Which can be a problem for colleges specifically as most run on strict NAT.
Overall rating - 7.5/10
It's a great fighting game, and a must buy for arcsys fans especially if you're a Blazblue player. Would rate higher if not for it's issues with the online function that I touched upon. Although, arcsys has been dishing out patches continuously to better improve the online as well as other bugs.
With the sequel "GGXrd Revelator" rolling around the corner in just a couple of months, this is a great opportunity for new players to give this game a shot.

After a Dozen Years comes now the next new Installment of Guilty Gear.
Developed with the Unreal Engine 3, the Game features now real 3D Chars (No HD Sprites) alongside some few Cinematics during Play which gives the Feel of Immersive 3D. The Game itself is still played in 2D (Arenas are tough 3D Maps with Impression giving 2D).
You can choose over 16 Characters (some New alongside some Old Ones) each with his own Challenge Course for learning BnB Combos. The Story Mode is now a Movie (estimated 4 hours) without some Interaction, so you can sit back and press only the Text Screens away during Talking between Characters.
For Singleplayer there is not much Content: M.O.M, Arcade, Story Mode, Challenges and Missions (BlazBlue in Comparison offers in that Regard more Gameplay for Singleplayer)
Network is like in BB by opening Lobbys for People to gather. As Host you have Options kicking out unwanted Guests or announcing disclosure of Room (Useful for a better Closure while others are finishing their Matches)
Here are some of my +/ o / - Points:
Positive:
- 1080p Support for gorgeous looking Fights
- 16 Chars to choose from which isnt that few since its newly developed
- Roman Cancel Mechanic was remade, so that FRC is possible for everyone (in GGXX FRC were limited and difficult to perform for Beginners (Hit FRC at 1/15 of a Second in a Frame!))
- M.O.M has more Depth than in GGXX (Comparable like the Abyss Mode in BB)
- Network Code is much better and has automatic Delay (GGXX AC+R used static Delay if i recall correctly)
- Videos in Story Mode gives you some Anime Feeling and is good to watch (Could also turn in a full fledget Anime IMHO)
- New Mechanics like Blitzshield for Counterattacking, etc.
- Connection and FPS Counter for Network Mode gives you good Infos if Match is possible
- Hellfire Mechanic (Higher Damage, etc.) gives you Motivation to continue when you reach Critical Health before loosing.
Neutral:
- Danger Time Mechanic can be annoying depending how you see it (20% more Damage if you get hit while being in Mortal Counter State with nearly no Teching!)
- Some Old Chars have gained/losed more Moves than other (Example: Axl/Ky getting better Moves, Slayer being ripped off of some vital Moves from AC+R, etc.)
- New Roman Cancel Mechanic and other Adjustements may be a Turn Down for Veterans from GGXX. Xrd has a more "casual" feeling to avoid a too high learning curve for Beginners
Negative:
- Low Content for Singleplayer
- No Survival Mode in Xrd
- Huge Damage Scaling. Some Combos can reduce nearly 3/4 of your Health Bar in one Combo Chain!!!
- OP DLC Chars in my Eyes (DLC Chars (Leo, Elphelt & Sin) have (very) high damage output)
Note: Sin/Elphelt got nerfed strongly in Revelator, which shows how unbalanced they are in Sign
- Few Old Chars nerfed strongly in Xrd (Slayer and Potemkin from Top Tier to Low Tier in Xrd)
- Rarely Bug: After committing to a Match, you get thrown out because Connection wasn't possible
Fazit:
I can wholeheartly recommend this Game for GG Fans and Newcomers.

I find it difficult to not recommend Super Cyborg because it's obviously a work of passion and a tribute to the old NES title 'Super Contra'
The graphics are suitably retro though they tend more to the garish EGA colours than the more muted NES pallette.  Turning off filtering and blending options gives a very old school emulated look that I find appealing.  The sprites are chunky and what they lack in style they make up for in character.  Curiously in this day-and-age the game is locked to a 4:3 ratio screen which leaves the borders black.
The music is generally good and has a remixed contra vibe going.  It doesn't quite have the presence of a lot of the late 80s games and as such is fairly forgettable; but this is not a significant criticism as it still suits the game.  The sound effects are very similar to Super Contra but - again - miss something vital and don't quite feel 'there'.
My biggest gripe is with the gameplay.  It's punishingly difficult in the later stages.  A frustration that's exacabated by the lack of a quick restart button.  Miss or lose a power up and that's the point at which the stage is failed, everything afterwards is just killing the player.
It's made more frustrating by a myriad of small differences from Super Contra.  Things that should have been fixed during playtesting.  The enemy bullets move too fast and being purple / yellow are difficult to spot agains purple or yellow backgrounds.  There are cheap deaths near the borders of the screen: enemies spawn underneath the player or shoot from outside the edges.
Couple this with a lack of checkpoints in some very long stages and it's time to start throwing controllers.
The controls are classic Contra though the player moves a bit more slowly than in the original.  The gun doesn't angle correctly up inclined platforms but this is hardly a problem.  What is a problem is that analogue controls on game controllers do not work; there is no diagonal fire with the analogue sticks.
To wrap this up.  If you're feeling nostalgic and want to mess around in a Super Contra like game for a couple of hours then buy Super Cyborg.  If you're looking for a platformer like Gryzor, Contra or Turrican then approach with caution; Super Cyborg is too frustrating to scratch that itch.

The Ace Combat series was for a long time my favorite series in the genre of Jet combat, and in many cases its the only series in the flight genre that has tried to find a nice balance between gameplay and realism. Ever since I first picked up and played Ace Combat 4 on the playstation 2 I have always been a fan of what ever project aces has done even though most of the titles in the playstion 2 and even 3 were very similar and really didn't bring anything new to the table, the past Ace Series titles and always gotten the most important platormer basics down. Fun combat, decent story telling, and a large variety of weapons, paint jobs, and fighters to trade missles with. While air to ground combat was never impressive, this never was the center of attention for fans of the series such as myself. Fun intense dogfights should always be the main focus in a series that has always been about jet on jet combat.
Ace Combat Assault Horizon is clearly an attempt by Namco and Project Aces to mix things up a bit and try to add and improve on the genre and for that goal in mind I applaud them for attempting to bring something new and fun to a genre that has not seen any real changes to gameplay other than improved graphics. The introduction of Helicopters, and gunships and the new dogfight mechanics were very intresting ideas, and since we have been in the middle of the summer video game drought I figured I would give this title a spin for nastagia's sake and see if the new game features were as fun as the trailers looked.
While I like the idea of the Dogfight mode and while it even looks pretty, the controls seem odd, clunky and poorly designed. Graphically stunning but it felt like it was to scripted at times and not natural. Helicopters were a huge disappointment. The machincs are almost outright broken and while it isn't always fair to compare titles I was hoping for gameplay closer to the feel of the Battlefield series of games.
Overall I want to like this game but its cluncky controls prevent me from being able to recommend the title.

Despite the onslaught of bullets and monsters to pay attention to, deaths very rarely feel cheap. Similarly to Volgarr the Viking, expect to repeat levels many times before becoming skilled enough to complete the game. And just completing one level feels like a big deal. Compared to Volgarr though, the pace of Super Cyborg is quicker, and difficulty maybe a touch easier. You'll still swear it's impossible many times.
I'm not very good at these games so i tend to hate them. Super Cyborg felt surprisingly encouraging. It's easy to play but everything kills in one hit so it's important to figure out how to deal with new enemies or sequences. The game stays fresh with new types of pain to put you through and even though i'd have to replay stages again and again, i was motivated to get through and see what the next pit of hell is gonna be like.
It's tough but fun, mostly because of really good gameplay/controls and a lack of repetitive elements. An excellent tribute to a different era that still feels good today. Well designed and polished, making an excellent use of the retro style. Sprinkled with evil.

Revolution tried to make Broken Sword into modern 3D graphics, which resulted in the game losing its incredible animated graphics and point and click aspect. But the story and characters remain great as in previous games. Puzzles changed into box moving and stealth passages with some action sequences. If you really want to know how the story continues and more about George and Nico, I would say, definitely play it, but you might be disappointed with the gameplay changes.

Nico is being framed for Homicide of the Hacker she was about to interview, while George arrived too late in Congo where the scientist who called him is being killed by a mysterious man and his thugs in an archeological site. Once again this Broken Sword Chapter begins on a rush and with some news as well. This is Another Point & Click that decided the old 2d system was obsolete and had to be renovated and replaced with a new 3d interface. Good thing? Bad thing? Well it's true that the old 2d interface is a classic best suited for adventures, but this is not just a matter of following a trend. New mechanics have been introduced, so even if the third dimension wasn't necessary it suits fine this adventure as the items you can interact with are easily marked and reachable, the character can move fluently, and the camera system has been studied enough to prevent as much as possible those classic shot troubles. The inventory system is quite comfortable and well integrated in the game (unlike Grim Fandango's, just to make an example) and the actions pad seems like a good integration as well: there are 4 slots which hold 4 different kind of interactions. According to the item, the compatible actions will lit and will be usable with the corresponding key.
The most important news still is the action side of the game: while in previous chapter you never needed to run now you can. And there are also stealth sections where running is mostly inadvisable as you'll be heard if you do it too close, so you'll need to quietly sneak behind guards and other things like these. And last, we have the infamous boxes... XD
In this chapter we have many situations and riddles that will require you to pull or push many boxes (or rocks, or other things) in different positions at the purpose of granting you a passage or maybe blocking some mechanism, or maybe even solving more complicated puzzles.
So it is safe to say that this chapter sees more action along with classic riddles and box riddles. As a confirm there are (few) Quick time events, not to mention the very end of the game which is a little action based (no spoilers, beside the gameplay), but there's nothing to worry about if you're not used to action games and prefer a quiet adventure, as every situation of this kind starts from a checkpoint, hence if you fail you can quickly restart from that point until you're able to pass through.
I've had some minor issues with the game, as I run it on Windows 10: the game kept on playing windowed, and I had a hard time to save my video resolution and settings as well, but these are minor issues to me as anything worse ever happened to prevent me from enjoying the game.
After all I enjoyed this chapter, the story was intricate but I liked it, The 3d interface was a change but has been handled well as it was quite easy to use, and about puzzles, as usual, some of them you have to try out of schemes. Anyways this is a good chapter, to me.

I really enjoyed this game back in the day (it was called Odium then). It had the same feel as a turn-based Resident Evil 1 (horror themed, mutants, scarce ammo and health). I hadn't been able to finish it back then so I decided to give it another try. I wasn't expecting it to work on Win10 without a hitch but, to my surprise, it did fairly well (choose the SW renderer).
I played in a way to conserve the most ammunition and health (and with proper branching saves) so I had ample of each toward the end. I even had more than necessary shotgun shells because I didn't pick up the shotgun at the beginning of the game.
Unfortunately, the game has a bug that prevents you from completing it - the enemy that throws plasma balls can't complete his turn so the game stalls. There might be a way to circumvent this problem though - I had the same problem in another battle and prevented it from happening by sacrificing health in order to immediately attack an enemy. I think DirectX function calls during some screen scroll events are causing the problem but I could be wrong.
Nevertheless, I did enjoy the game.
PRO:
Theme and mechanics (Resident Evil alike)
Acceptable plot
Difficulty
CON:
No HW renderer support (not really a problem because the game literally takes seconds to launch)
Bugs that stall the battles (possibly circumventable)
Forced perspective, in other words, the vanishing points are too close (this causes distortions that make judging distances difficult)
18 years later and its still one of my favourite turn based games.

===
Gorky 17 is a very old and rather obscure RPG of a now distant era, and is set in an abandoned, secret Russian facility where myusterious experiments are conducted; you will be in command of an elite NATO task force with orders to find what happened there and retrieve certain items. It features a fixed storyline with no branching choices as most RPGs have nowadays, open environments to explore, loot and character progression systems, and turn-based grid combat. Even if this game has not many elements of the modern era, it is still a decent title: the setting is very dark and well made, the fights are challenging, and there is good diversity of situations and enemies to encounter. It is not very long for being an RPG, but still you can have a great deal of fun.
===
+ Good old-fashioned, dark, gritty style of setting and environment, they don't make these anymore.
+ Decent variety of enemies and encounter situations
+ Decent amount of weapons and loot in general, but rather than quantity purpose of loot is favored in this game
+ Good level of challenge, you need to strategize quite a bit to be successful and save ammo / resources
+ Very hidden secrets that can lead to great rewards
+ The characters are decent-ish but will make you have a laugh or two, sometimes
- On modern systems the game requires DgVoodoo plugin to run properly, see the Community Hub to know about this
- Very restricted exploration
- No possibility of choices in the story
- Some situations / mechanics are not properly explained and can lead to confusion / frustration sometimes
- Rather limited character progression, where also some statistics are useless (like Max HP, it's useless!)
- Rather short longevity for an RPG (finished it in around 12 hours)
===
Gorky 17 may not be a  masterpiece of the genre but offers a quite unique setting and some fun for oldschool RPG lovers and also horror fans. The strategy involved in combats is still good and provides lots of fun to overcome encounters and having to change strategies at every encounter to face different enemies. If you find this on sale i say why not buying it cheap, it can be a good title if you like the genre.

It's a shame that there's really so little to say when a fighting game does everything right. Words like "satisfying" sound a little trite and hollow considering the tremendous effort that goes into a fighter that delivers what you expect from a worthy entry to the genre. Guilty Gear Xrd is, quite simply, one of the best fighters out there right now, let alone one of the best fighters available on this distribution platform. As you'd expect from this series, the visuals are gorgeous, the sound is killer, the community is decent, and the basic mechanics are easy enough for a novice to pick up and enjoy. The Tutorial and Mission modes in this game are an outstanding introduction to Xrd's new elements (For those of us who need to be broken of the bad habits we picked up in AC) as well as a great platform for newcomers to improve not only in this game, but fighting games in general. If you're one of those guys that cut your teeth on #Reload's multiplayer, you'll be at home in rather short order.
That said, it's not perfect. The character roster is disappointingly lean, and the learning curve for a considerable number of those characters available is startlingly high. The multiplayer interface is unintuitive garbage, and in general, too much of Xrd's metagame takes place in corners for my liking. I personally still prefer AC+R for these reasons, but not by a significant enough margin to abandon either game. Get Xrd, play the Tutorial, jump in, and I think you'll have a good time.

Long Live the Queen looks like it might be easy to dismiss as just another visual novel. It's not. At all.
The better way to describe this game's genre is as a
. And that distinction makes a ton of difference.
The reason it's a roguelike is because you are stuck with the consequences of your actions. There's no  going back. No re-assigning points (which you get from the RPGish training system within the game). You make choices and you can die. Permanently. In fact there are many different ways to die, some of which are very hard to find and you have to try for.
There's a brutalism here that is tempered by comedy. Some of the situations and things happening are absurd, and the game recognizes that. But it's also totally unforgiving. You can't win a sword fight if you've never trained with a sword. But you can use your magic skills to just blast a sword-wielding opponent away. This blend of campy and fun and serious all at the same time really sets the tone for the game.
I replayed it repeatedly after finally beating it the first time, just for fun. And also to try to explore all the other branches that I missed the first time around. It's rewarding, engrossing, and I ended up spending way more time on this game than I ever thought I would.
The achievements unlock in weird ways: some of them won't register until you've attained it, then quit the game, then restarted it. I don't know why but it can be confusing and frustrating when you think you unlocked something but it doesn't pop.
My biggest complaint is really with the beginning of the game: there are only a few paths that work to get you past the early pitfalls. It would be nice if there were more variety in how you could handle those situations. But it's kind of the nature of the beast: since all your skills start at zero it inevitably takes time to build them up to be anything useful.
There are also some skills that almost never come up. Animal handling? They might be pivotal for a single check in the entire game. It would've been nice if they were replaced with something more interesting, or just used more.
So if you want a unique, fun experience where you play a teenage queen trying to run a medieval country, complete with noble plots, wars, romance, and magic, then look no further.

There were some major changes to the franchise on this game, particularly the controls. No mouse at all, everything is done on the keyboard. At first I really disliked the controls, but you can't deny there's a simplistic ease to them. There's no hint system, but because everything is so linear, there's not really much you need to figure out so you don't need hints. Like always, the plot and the characters are wonderful, the best part of Broken Sword games are always the interesting if not always coherent story lines. There are a ton of timing/movement puzzles and man, are you gonna get sick of moving boxes. They added some more comedic characters and these were a welcome addition.

When I first played this game, I hated it. I loved the 2D animation and the point and click interface of the first two Broken Sword games. This was so different that the experience was almost ruined for me. I'm glad I saw it through, because this is a great game. We still have the George and Nico that we have loved from the previous games (same voice actors and a great script) and the story is great, stemming back to the first Broken Sword game. The 3D is decent, with some awesome set pieces, and the rest being average. The controls can take a bit to get used to, and may turn off a lot of people. A point and click adventure has turned into an only use your keyboard adventure. That was difficult for me to swallow at first. For the most part, the puzzles are pretty good.....except....for all...the BOXES!! There were way too many move-the-box puzzles. One here or there isn't a sin, but the amount in here makes them feel like filler, as if the game needed to be longer. I don't think the game would have suffered had they removed some of these tedious box puzzles. A minor complaint is that there are moments in the game in which you have just moments to react, and you have to press the right button to avoid death. It kind of kills when the button doesn't appear till after you die. Luckily, the game loads right back to the perilous situation and you now know what button to push. This doesn't happen often though, so it is a minor annoyance.  This game will probably not be considered as good as the first two, but it is definitely still worth playing. There is enough Broken Sword goodness to soften the leap from 2D to 3D adventure.

After exactly 60 minutes playing DD and countless hours playing other TD games, here are my thoughts.
I finished the first level (40 waves) after 2 tries. It felt long and I wanted it to be over sooner. 30 minutes is way too long for a round of td to last unless its endless mode or something like SC2 Arcade Squadron TD where multiplayer is involved.
The graphics are pretty good a solid 8/10 for td games.
I like that you can generally place towers wherever you want. but I don't like that the path is set and there's no mazing.
You get upgrade points every 5 waves that let you boost a tower. I used Tesla so I took "hits 2 targets" at 5 and 3 targets at 10 , 15 is a waste with no bonus just to unlock "advanced" bonuses such as +10% range damage or attack spd. By wave 40 I had +20% damage, +20% Attack Speed and Tesla hits 3 targets. Maybe if the upgrades came every 2-3 waves it would be more engaging but as it was they seemed limited. There is so much more potentail for a progression tree here that I feel is currently wasted... Points every level or 2 and many more perks to choose from and branch off of would make it a lot less bland.
I really want to like it and I think it has a ton of potentail, but things like a 10 wave mode, more progression, permanent progression of some sort beteween levels, tuning of tower and upgrade costs, rewards for completing levels besides just unlocking the next map, more maps... could help a lot.
I also note that the game seems to be lacking music and only has sound effects. No biggie really but I noticed it was odd that it was silent and I had to go into the options just to turn the sound effects on. I actually appreciate the developer trying to save me the hassle of muting bad music so I can play my own but I had never seen this done before so it threw me a bit as I thought my speakers must be muted or something.
Right now I'm not sure if playing through another long map is worth the cost of admission. I don't get anything for it really that I can tell besides a new map to play on and apparently there are only like 12 maps, so, thats like a dollar for every path puzzle to beat and then the local multiplayer that will take too long to really play with any local friends.
Basically it feels like it's got something charming about it and I do like it, but, it's just not grabbing me and feels like it needs a little more substance to get out of the tablet clone realm and into the full on steam PC TD realm where I want it to be. it's not bad but it's not great either... I'm in between recommending or not. I think I have to say no at it's current price point for what it is. but with a little love this could really be a fun gem.

A very solid, balanced, and timeless Street Fighter game.
Where as newer fighters (Street Fighter V, MvC3, Street Fighter vs Tekken) feel like games of checkers, Street Fighter IV holds its own and plays like a game of chess. The game provides a variety of characters, each unique in their balanced set of strategic advantages/tactical allowances, and allows players to really discover that one character that matches their preferred style of play. The game does require investing some time to gain an understanding of the game's mechanics, level design, tactics commonly used by other players with each character, and their preferred character/character's core, but the time will pay off as you'll feel a greater sense of gratification and appreciation for the game and other players with each spar you engage in.
Street Fighter IV is a game of SKILL. It requires the abilities to read one's opponents, quick reflexes, and the timely precision in executing inputs/deploying tactics. As mentioned many 2D fighters nowadays play like checkers in the sense that the bar for entry has been set too low for the sake of reaching a wider market and as a result increase profit generation. They feel as if the only worth they have is to those who want instant gratification in playing something that is easily accessible and off the bat sets an unbalanced win-loss ratio to their favor, leaning towards 'win'. This is apparent with MvC3's dedicated launch button and semi-unbreakable air combos that require a cheap guessing game of rock-paper-scissors to break out of. Street Fighter V and Street Fighter vs Tekken are also guilty of similar mundane juggling/gambling mechanics that one would expect to be integrated in the likes of a Mortal Kombat or a mobile game whose purposes and selling points are based on spetacle, cheap thrills, and the instant release of dopamine.
The list of criticisms, for the above mentioned games, goes on and on (lets not get started on the gem system/shortcuts in SFxTekken), but if you want a game that is fun, entertaining, requires critical strategic/tactical thinking, and brings a sense of fulfillment with each match, Street Fighter IV is the cream of the crop.
Ultra Street Fighter IV is a must-own title for anyone who likes fighting games. It may not be the biggest or the best, but it is a very well-rounded package with more to offer than most.

Like text based games? Like games where you can die alot? Well lo and behold, Long Live the Queen. With various other nobles out to kill you after your Mother suddenly passes away, it's up to you to build up your stats like in the Princess Maker series. Those who know the brutality of old politics should know what to expect (with a side of sorcery). With various plotlines and deaths possible. This game is sure to keep you busy for awhile.

This is by far my favourite game in my library. I was never into visual novels, and really didn't like story based games, but something in Long Live the Queen is different. Perhaps it's the progression of the character from a sniveling little princess to warlord, or perhaps it's the sheer challenge of living to the end. I personally beleive I love this game for the variety of ways to play. There are many ways to succeed and even more ways to die. I'm 2 hours in and can see many many hours more. Once you beat it, there's a desire to beat it another way, with different skills, or have "the perfect game".
10/10

Fun, if a bit grindy. If you are playing the original State of Decay, then Zombie Standard Time is a must so that half your guys don't get eaten/commit suicide/get lost while you are not playing. ZST lets you control exactly how much time passes while you are not playing (or forces time not to pass at all), so that alleviates some frustration.
Besides ZST, you may want to drop by State of Decay Nexus and grab the following mods:
- SweetFX for State of Decay - improves palette and shadows.
- Real flashlight - just what it says on the tin.
- Powerhouse and Reflexes - gives the more physically gifted characters a chance to dip into both Powerhouse and Reflexes skill tree, making them a lot better (it's a joy watching Marcus roundhouse-kick a bunch of zeds in the face and then ruin their day with Wrestling or a big sledgehammer).
- Melee and Ranged - some characters can develop both the melee and ranged specializations (also helpful).
The game isn't without downsides, graphics are not exactly top of the line (though quite passable); a lot of stuff happens at the same time while you play (the radio girl keep chiming in every five seconds with new missions and you end up overwhelmed), there are some bugs with clipping and getting stuck, but overall it's worth to buy if it's on sale.

has it all: isometric perspective, the plot of a B-movie, repetitive yet weirdly addictive combat, and more than enough challenge.
So you’ve been dumped in the middle of a god-forsaken and monster-infested ghost of a city and have to fight your way through hordes of mutants to get to the truth of the matter. As said before, the plot certainly is not the game’s major selling point. The bulk of the dialogue consists of your burly man-soldiers either grunting action-movie clichés or stating the obvious, but I’d be lying if I said I didn’t have a soft spot for this ragged band of gun-toting alpha males by the end.
Graphically, the game is a mixed bag. The 3D models and animations are a clunky collection of fist-sized pixels while the FMV sequences look like someone made a stop-motion video with LEGO puppets. I also found the monster design to be quite unimaginative; they mostly look like giant bugs with the occasional robot parts attached to them.
However, the prerendered backgrounds is where the game still shines. The complete carnage of abandoned buildings, piled-up car wrecks, the subtle light effects; they all make the desolation of Gorky come alive. It really looks like something diabolical hit this town hard and now lurks in the shadows, preying on you.
The battles, as said, are rather repetitive, yet oddly fun and rewarding. It’s all pretty straight forward: walk, attack, defend, heal, exploit weakness, kill stuff with fire… Every now and then there is a boss battle or an extra objective such as preventing a friendly NPC from dying. Because of rather arbitrary restrictions to the use of weapons (for example: guns can only fire in four directions, shotguns in eight) it sometimes feels as if you’re playing a weaponized version of chess (i.e.: not being able to hit someone standing right freaking next to you…).
Your characters can level up their stats, but since there are no random encounters and you cannot sell or buy items, the appeal was lost to me. The battles you fight are often tough and resources are sparse, but many players have commented on the fact that the game is actually quite easy when you play it again.
One minor gripe that deserves mentioning: every now and then, the plot demands that one of your party members either die or run off. When this happens, they take all their inventory with them. I was rather dismayed when I saved right after a death scene, only to later discover that I also had to say goodbye to some of my best weapons and healing items.
Long story short, the game has its faults and at times I found it to be too difficult, but it was great to play this old-timer.

It's like being 10 again and playing Gryzor with a buddy in front of a NES and a CRT TV, except now I'm over 30 and playing in a big♥♥♥♥♥monitor, using a 360 controller and skype to play from far away.

Were you a fan of Contra when it hit arcades?  Were you a fan of Contra when it was ported to consoles?  Have you been a fan of contra since the begining, or were even newly introduced to the game, lured by challenge and generally fun gameplay?  Well, I cannot recommend this game more for you.  It captures the spirit of contra, it and provides quite the enjoyable experience.
I would give this game a 10 out of 10, but there is one part of the game that is really holding it back from greatness.  I don't care what your opinions or intentions were in designing stage 6 of this game, but there is and will not be an excusable reason to include THE WORST ASPECTS OF SUPER CONTRA AND CONTRA 3!  As a matter of fact, every game in the contra series to embrace the "top down shooter" model as been a dismall failure because it simply is not fun, no matter how easy it may be.  This game, did not make the top down stage fun either.  I would go so far as to recommed scrapping the stage all together.  Just make the cut, and render the game 6 stages long.  Or go the extra mile, and give us another side scrolling platformer stage.
The stage didn't work in any of the games the devs clearly pulled inspiration from, and nostalgia for the sake of nostalgia is never a winning business model, especially when it is painful nostalgia (IE, I will not play super contra again because of these stages).  They are terrible, they break the paradigm of gameplay that is established in the stages leading up to them, and following them, and the pace of the game is dropped to an almost litteral crawl when you get to them.  They are so jarring.
That being the case, the music in the game is amazing.  The sprite work, is top notch, and the levels are fricken cool to play through (barring stage 6... it was just boring to play through).
Stage 6 wouldn't be so bad, were it not so damn long.  I mean, it is literally the length of 2 stages put together, and even comes complete with check points (which is not excusing or making the stage out to be better than it could be, make no mistake...)
All things considered, the game is awsome.  It is a solid release, that I have not been able to break in any of the time I have been playing.  The bosses were clever (albe it incredibly frustrating to figure out at times), and I am currently looking into the harder difficulties the game has to offer.  Normal mode, is actually pretty difficult by comparison to other games of this genre.
I am not sure the game required a save feature that saves your game at check points.  It does kinda... make the game much easier to be able to keep repeating from where you last saved.  Part of the charm of the games this game is inspired from, are that by the time you make it past stage 7, you have mastered stages 1-6.  This game just allows you to fumble past each stage and get lucky in some cases, powering through your lives in hopes that you can barely beat the boss of the stage and get to the check point.
All and all though, it is worth the investment, and comes complete with Netplay so you can play with friends from a distance so you won't get punched in the shoulder or face when you jump the screen to high, and burn their last life.
Pick this game up.  Its worth the money, if this genre of action platformer is your cup of tea.

Super Cyborg is a very polished Contra-styled arcade run and gun shooter. It controls identical to Contra in terms of movement, shooting, and jump physics. Level design is also extremely reminiscient of Contra.
Super Cyborg plays really well, with lots of very varied level and boss designs. It's playstyle is much closer to the older Contra's, as it emphasizes platforming and constantly moving forward over the "boss rush" style gameplay of later titles (see: Hardcorps, Shattered Soldier, and many Treasure titles). I found this refreshing, since I like the constant push forward in older titles.
It is much harder then the older Contras however, and not in the way I would have liked. I'm an arcade game veteran who's 1 life cleared Ninja Gaiden, Ghouls and Ghosts, and various shmups, and I have to say that this game requires an absurd amount of memorization. Usually, I play these sorts of games on one credit, restarting from the beginning when I game over, but this sort of playstyle is not feasible for Super Cyborg until you've learned the whole game. You need a plan and a route for every stage after the first 3, so you'll definitely want to grind some of the stages for a while with unlimited continues if you want to clear this game.
I'm also a bit more partial to challenges based on reflexes and improvisation. I always enjoyed Contra 1-3 and Ghouls and Ghosts because many of the enemy behaviors were extremly randomized and required on the spot reflexes instead of just planning. Super Cyborg has a few spots like this, but it's much more static and memorization focused in general. If you like formulating plans and routes for strategic gameplay, you'll likely enjoy this, but it's not quite to my tastes.
Overall, I like SC quite a bit. It does a lot of great things, and its platforming focus is a breath of fresh air for run and gun shooters. It's not quite my ideal run and gun shooter, but it's definitely worth it for fans of the genre.

Do you like Contra? Do you like 8-bit/16-bit games? Do you like difficult arcade games that will bring your patience so down that you'll want to throw the gamepad againts the screen?
Then Super Cyborg is your game.
As a fan of the Contra series, I can only but recommend this game and, if possible, use a old console gamepad replica (or a converter with an original SNES) to play it. Gameplay is perfect, graphics are awesome, music makes you feel back to the ending eighties and online Co-op is the best addition this game needed. Thumbs ups for Super Cyborg!

I purchased this title when it first came out and casually played it off and on as it was updated. In its earlier stages I would have recommended the game just because it was successful at making you feel that you were actually playing a survival game. You started out with a handful of items including a water bottle that would get you to the beginning of day 3, if you were unlucky at finding a bucket for water by then you died.
Unlike now, buckets were primarily found in shipwrecks that littered the ocean floor and provided a good bit of exploration as you scooted a long in your raft and saw a broken mast sticking up and dived down to search the cabnets and lockers inside the ship. You were instantly pitted against the sharks as you dodged them in between surfacing for air and diving back into the ship to collect the loot. When you got to your raft you weren't safe, the sharks were actually good at tipping over your raft and dumping you back into the water giving you a nice panic attack as you tried to flip your raft back over and get on it before being eaten alive.
The updates they have made since then have made some of the things about the game better, but they have also ruined a lot of what was making the game interesting. You don't see large ships sunken in deep water like you used to, as most seem to be half a ship already parked up on a beach for you. The previously coveted bucket is now everywhere on the islands, in my last go at this game I visited maybe 3 different islands and already found 7-8 buckets. If i had even 2 buckets after 10 in game days of play previously I would have considered it a solid session. It was just enough to give you what you needed to keep going, but also not so much that you still had to manage your time and precious daylight doing things that were actually going to let you live another day.
As of the time of this review 2/13/17, you will find more than you ever need to survive endlessly in this game in the first 20 minutes of starting a new game. This I guess isn't totally bad but they do not offer you any other game design to replace the hardcore survival aspect. There is no progression, no skills or talents that you slowly grind for to figure out how to make things better and no where interesting to go. Would be a great direction change for them to redesign the entire map of this game and how it is generated, small island perfectly placed X distance apart in each compass direction isn't interesting. Starting out in a small chain of the current sized islands while you slowly build up enough resources and skills to craft a decent raft to sail to a larger more populated island with several interesting locations, landmarks, caves and mysteries to explore would be a delight compaired to what is currently offered in the game world.

The first thing that has to be said is that this game isn't in the slightest as hilarious as the trailer.
Is it a bad game though? Not at all, I thoroughly enjoy it!
That said, if you're in for a funny and light-hearted story this isn't the game for you. When I bought the game I was expecting exactly that, having a good time watching Elodie die in the most ridiculous ways possible. There are "only" 11 ways to die though, some easier to achieve than others and all rather far in-between.
Long Live The Queen is fun on other levels though, especially if you're into vast lore and royal family trees; it took me a few hours before I could keep the different duchies and their representatives apart. Intruige is what really drives this game in my oppinion. People try backstabbing Elodie left and right, and more often than killed I saw her removed from her throne or exiled. And when I finally made her queen in one of my runs Elodie was so hardend she ended up torturing her maid because her love interest (a commoner) rather fled the country than mary the cruel Queen. Well, all that happened after the people cheerfully lynched magic wielders all around the country and assasins killed the closest relatives Elodie had left - on her own order, of course. As you can see, all in all a very happy game.
Gameplay-wise it's your standard visual novel with lessons in the mornings and afternoons, weekends to relax and change the mood, which will effect Elodies potential to learn certain skills, and "cut scenes" where you have to decide her actions to steer the story in a certain direction depending if the skill check fails or succeeds. There are major plot moments that appear every run but others depend strongly on your decisions/skills. There are characters and places I haven't seen yet, even after 13h of gameplay. If you are someone who's very keen on getting every single acchievement in their games you'll have tons of hours ahead of you - when not relying on walkthroughs, that is.
So, if you're in for everything above, all I have left to say is good luck making Elodie queen!
Also, I enjoyed the music. Classic piano, simple but catchy.

I've been playing Street Fighter for as long as I can remember.  My earliest memory is of one of my uncles and my older brother scrubbing it up as Sagat and Dictator in SF2 Turbo for the SNES.  I've never really been an arcade rat, but I've played Street Fighter on console pretty consistently my entire life.  Being one of the few kids who got a Sega Saturn helped out with that.
Alpha 2 on Saturn is godlike.  Fighting games were godlike.  That is until 2003 or so and Capcom♥♥♥♥♥♥the bed and started putting out dumb ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t like the Harvey Birdman game and those remedial light gun editions of Resident Evil.  They were going to put out this game called Capcom Fighting Allstars, but I guess somebody was afraid of making too much money and they pussied out.   Maybe nobody over there thought fighting games were popular anymore.  I don't know.  Didn't stop them from putting out that Sengoku Basara fighting game in Japan.  Meanwhile, most of us here in the states didn't really know about King of Fighters or Guilty Gear and were relegated to playing Tekken and the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ 3D Mortal Kombats for a while.
That's alright, though, because in 2008 Street Fighter 4 came out to ignite new hope and excitement for what was becoming a niche genre.  It's too bad Capcom didn't ditch their old habit of releasing multiple versions of the same game by the time it came out.   I understand that they do it because that's the way arcade machines work.  I also understand that reactive balancing can severely frustrate the pro community.  Still, for your average Sally Lunchpail, this kind of♥♥♥♥♥♥puts a serious strain on the wallet.   If you count Arcade Edition 2012, Ultra is the fourth iteration, and the bonuses it adds are basically just flipped assets from X Tekken and a pallette swap of Cammy.  But later on, they added a mode where the characters have weird moves, so I guess everything's cool.  At least it's not like Ultra Street Fighter 2, where they're taking a defibrilator to that dead horse by just adding more shotos.
I digress.  If you happen to like Street Fighter 2, you'll probably like Street Fighter 4.  It's got all the same stuff, including all of the characters and then some.  Where the older games introduced totally different casts with each roster,  Street Fighter 4 is more like the greatest hits album of fighting games.  Now with bonus tracks that no one really cares about, like Hakan and Rufus.
Also, if you're a masochist, you'll probably enjoy playing this game online.  I have like 35 hours on the steam version of Ultra, but I've been playing Street Fighter IV since vanilla on console.  I've no doubt logged hundreds of hours, if not thousands.  I no lifed Arcade Edition for a while.  That's the kind of thing you do when you work a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ dead end job because the only academic field you're interested in is literature, and there's no real point going to college for it.  So yeah, I'd spend hours in training mode, trying to get better.  Jonesing for a win.  Even if you're a loser in life, you can be a winner in Street Fighter.  Except for me apparently.  Maybe I can't get my brain and my thumbs won't cooperate.  Maybe my background in literature left me too dumb not to fall for stupid ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t tactics.  Whatever it is, I can't seem to get a win most nights.  If you're new to the game, you won't either.  Most of the time, when you do manage to get the upper hand, the scrubby ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ you're walloping will most often rage quit at the last minute to rob you of any progress.  That's why you have to be a masochist.
But don't go away thinking of this as a negative review.  Street Fighter 4 is a comfortable game to play, after a while.  You get used to the rhythm of matches.  The familiar characters insure that even a complete beginner will have someone simple enough to play.  (Unless your entire fighting game background is in Smash Brothers or something.  Then, you're pretty much ♥♥♥♥ed.)  Some of the remixes of the music is pretty good.  Juri's theme is pretty good.  Poison is a pretty killer addition to the roster, and a lot of fun to play.  There are tons of modded skins out there if you're into that kind of thing.  Online, much like working a crappy fast food job for minimum wage, you won't make much progress for a long time, but at least you've rolled out of bed and done something.
TL;DR 9/10  Definite must play for fighting game fans.

This game is maximum badass to the maximum. As someone who has played way too much Super C on NES, this game has some guts. I found this game on Recently Released page when the game got released. At first it looked like any other random indie scrubbity scrub but as the trailer went on and showed the gameplay, it was pretty clear that I have to try this right away.
Super Cyborg has some heavy inspiration from Super C (or Probotector 2, since our heroes are robots) which is a good thing for my point of view due Super C did improve the game in so many ways compared to original NES Contra. Better jump physics, top down levels, mid-bosses and non-spread weapons are actually powerful. This is exactly what Super Cyborg has but with some extra spice on it.
You can for example lock your position so you can shoot any direction you want without moving. This is insanely handy when you want to fire diagonally without running back and fourth for example when fighting against stationary turrets. Super Cyborg also has an ability to charge your weapon (it has own button for it) which adds some damage to the shot. Pretty useful against bosses to get that accurate damage going.
Speaking of bosses, there are two types of bosses in this game. There are bosses that are trial and error and there are bosses that actually requires you to be awake and focus on the battle. While trial and error bosses aren't too nice, they are definitely much better than Super C bosses that were insanely boring and easily the weakest point of the game.
This game also supports online co-op which is very nice. Unfortunately I only have one friend that won't lose all his lives on the first level and he lives at the other side of the globe which this game does not like at all. I highly recommend getting a friend that is pretty close to you (read: region) to enjoy online co-op the fullest.
Super Cyborg is a great game, but it won't get a perfect score from me. There are some areas in the game that requires you to have a powerful weapon or you have going to have insanely bad time. Good example is the rolling corpse ball thing in final level. If you are unable to get the spread in there and you have playing with default gun instead, it gets insanely tricky since you can't hit the ball diagonally unless you are about to get hit by it. It could be me just being bad but any powerup before that section would be nice.
One of the features I would like to see in this game is the ability to go back to level 1 from the game over screen. In Super C the game goes back to title screen after 3 game overs but in order to start all over again in Super Cyborg, you have to go back to the menu and then make a new game which takes a bit more time than just pressing "Restart Game" or something. I find it a good way to try perfecting earlier levels and get prepared for later levels better.
I'm actually amazed how Super Cyborg hasn't gotten any showlight from Steam. People don't even know this game is being sold in Steam which is a real bummer. Super Cyborg is a hidden, rough looking gem and while apparently it has been out in Desura for some time, it was my personal GOTY for 2015.
So do I recommend this game to you? If you have played too much Contra/Super C, this is a must buy. Don't even think about it, go for it. For everybody else, you can download a demo and try it. It's a difficult game but success always will be rewarded.

The weapons are all the classic Contra 1 weapons, you have your M powerup, for machinegun which is basically a much faster and more powerful version of your basic gun, S spreadshot which is pretty self explanatory, E for electric shot which is a reskin of the original fire burst shot (and IMO makes more sense) and L for laser (Protip: rapidly hit the shot button with this weapon for DEVASTATING results). There's also a R powerup which adds rapidfire to whatever you're currently using. They added a couple of interesting twists, the weapons all have alternate fire modes that are basically charged up power shots, and there are hidden power ups in the levels. (I have yet to find these "hidden powerups" but they're hinted at in the achievements.
There's both local and online coop which is a great feature, this kind of game is best enjoyed with a friend. Online coop is handled via user hosted lobbys, but I have yet to play with anyone so I can't honestly say how well that handles.
You can also change the color and sprite (albeit a minimal change) of your character which is also a rather nice feature. The detail on the boss sprites is incredible and you can really get a feel of the "grotesque alien mutation look" they were going for. My only complaint when it comes to the enemy design is that certain enemies look pretty lackluster, like the eyeball enemies in the first 2nd and 3rd stages in particular.
Gameplay wise, the controls feel solid and precise and can be adjusted to suit just about any taste. You can even adjust your x and y axis which is somewhat rare for a side scroller. The level designs flow well, and you have a pretty decent chance to see what's trying to kill you before it gets a chance. There are 3 levels of difficulty and there's a significant difference between the 3. I don't recommend you play on normal alone unless you have VERY good reflexes or you're a glutton for pinishment. Boss patterns change with difficulty so there's an incentive to replay in that regards.
I recommend this game to fans of Contra or side scrollers in general. the price is right and it's quite fun.

This game has the best frustration-balance I ever encountered in a game.
Build up to counter the death you just experienced, just to die even earlier this time because you did not train something you did on last try. It's possible to beat it without a guide, but you need either an extreme amount of luck, or very many playthroughs to get it right, and as someone who build myself up through a high number of playthroughs, I don't think I've ever been so satisfied with beating a game before. And by beating I mean not dying.
You play princess Elodie on her last weeks before being crowned a queen after the tragic death of her mother. Your goal is to survive until then. Apparently you're safe forever if you're a queen, even though you can die from absolutely anything before then.
You build up her day by taking her to lessons.  You earn outfits that give bonuses to some stats. Your mood gives bonuses and disadvantages for learning certain lessons and doing a sparetime activity in the castle changes Elodie's mood. You can be a master tactician of every type or war and then die from poisoned chocolate. Having 0 knowledge actually mean 0 knowledge for Elodie and she does the dumbest things if she gets in a situation she knows nothing about. Creates a lot of humour in the game.
If you want every achievement you absolutely must use a guide to get the right skills at the right times, through many playthroughs. The game is more enjoyable if you play it to be crowned through knowledge you earn through many tries.
The game seems complicated at first try, but you easily get into it and learn to juggle skills, moods, classes, and, of course, dresses.
I recommend it, but be prepared for frustration, though you'll pull through because of the humour of the absurd deaths and the cutesyness of the game and music.

This game is excellent. I bought it when it was on sale during '14s Summer Sale, and I never regretted my purchase. This game has the perfect blend of difficulty and moe, to where it doesn't feel like you are skating along with no problems, but just enough difficulty to add to replay value. With a ton of different endings and options (even deaths!) this game can seriously be played over and over again.

The game is easier than the trailer makes it to be- very seldom do you need a seemingly useless skill. There is some trial and error (much more if you're trying to 100% it), but mostly just common sense mixed with a vaguely general idea how European feudal court politics operated are all you need to get pretty far on a blind run (if not beat it). Magic is completely overpowered once you level it up, which isn't hard, and isn't needed to beat the game. The biggest pain is figuring out which moods give what bonuses/penalties when learning stats. This visual novel has some decent replay value despite the linear story- the minor variances on successive playthroughs add up fairly well.

It's funny; I remember hating this game as a kid. And I don't mean that in the sense of, "Ugh, another random battle?" kind of hate, I mean I effing HATED it. I liked the story, interesting characters popped up, and I was really engaged in finding out the answers to the questions posed throughout, but it was, for a nine-year-old, impossible. Which is exactly what I love about it as an adult. Every move of every team member in every battle counts. If you take a defensive pose with a character and aren't attacked on the enemy's turn, you'll kick yourself for not healing instead. If you end your turn facing the wrong way, an enemy might flank you for a damage bonus. If you position two characters too close, some attacks may hurt them both. All of these factors, as well as far more, can mean the difference between victory and defeat. You could very well die in the first few battles, but even then you gain valuable information about the enemy's tactics. Not for the casual turn-based fan. If you liked Gladius, this one's a must-have.

I've been playing Street Fighter for as long as I can remember.  My earliest memory is of one of my uncles and my older brother scrubbing it up as Sagat and Dictator in SF2 Turbo for the SNES.  I've never really been an arcade rat, but I've played Street Fighter on console pretty consistently my entire life.  Being one of the few kids who got a Sega Saturn helped out with that.
Alpha 2 on Saturn is godlike.  Fighting games were godlike.  That is until 2003 or so and Capcom♥♥♥♥♥♥the bed and started putting out dumb ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t like the Harvey Birdman game and those remedial light gun editions of Resident Evil.  They were going to put out this game called Capcom Fighting Allstars, but I guess somebody was afraid of making too much money and they pussied out.   Maybe nobody over there thought fighting games were popular anymore.  I don't know.  Didn't stop them from putting out that Sengoku Basara fighting game in Japan.  Meanwhile, most of us here in the states didn't really know about King of Fighters or Guilty Gear and were relegated to playing Tekken and the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ 3D Mortal Kombats for a while.
That's alright, though, because in 2008 Street Fighter 4 came out to ignite new hope and excitement for what was becoming a niche genre.  It's too bad Capcom didn't ditch their old habit of releasing multiple versions of the same game by the time it came out.   I understand that they do it because that's the way arcade machines work.  I also understand that reactive balancing can severely frustrate the pro community.  Still, for your average Sally Lunchpail, this kind of♥♥♥♥♥♥puts a serious strain on the wallet.   If you count Arcade Edition 2012, Ultra is the fourth iteration, and the bonuses it adds are basically just flipped assets from X Tekken and a pallette swap of Cammy.  But later on, they added a mode where the characters have weird moves, so I guess everything's cool.  At least it's not like Ultra Street Fighter 2, where they're taking a defibrilator to that dead horse by just adding more shotos.
I digress.  If you happen to like Street Fighter 2, you'll probably like Street Fighter 4.  It's got all the same stuff, including all of the characters and then some.  Where the older games introduced totally different casts with each roster,  Street Fighter 4 is more like the greatest hits album of fighting games.  Now with bonus tracks that no one really cares about, like Hakan and Rufus.
Also, if you're a masochist, you'll probably enjoy playing this game online.  I have like 35 hours on the steam version of Ultra, but I've been playing Street Fighter IV since vanilla on console.  I've no doubt logged hundreds of hours, if not thousands.  I no lifed Arcade Edition for a while.  That's the kind of thing you do when you work a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ dead end job because the only academic field you're interested in is literature, and there's no real point going to college for it.  So yeah, I'd spend hours in training mode, trying to get better.  Jonesing for a win.  Even if you're a loser in life, you can be a winner in Street Fighter.  Except for me apparently.  Maybe I can't get my brain and my thumbs won't cooperate.  Maybe my background in literature left me too dumb not to fall for stupid ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t tactics.  Whatever it is, I can't seem to get a win most nights.  If you're new to the game, you won't either.  Most of the time, when you do manage to get the upper hand, the scrubby ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ you're walloping will most often rage quit at the last minute to rob you of any progress.
