Dark Souls has a reputation of being a hard and punishing; it worries me that people who haven't played this game think it might be too hard and would miss out on a genuinely fun game.
Dark Souls is not hard, it is challenging; the game has never felt unfair and I've never felt like I've died without deserving it. But I don't want to focus on the difficulty of the game, because I don't feel that the game's difficulty is what defines it.
Dark Souls is an incredible RPG with outstanding level design. I've never played a game that feels more rewarding to level up your character and aquire new and unique weapons that become more and more powerful as they scale with how you level your character. There are a large amount of possiblities on what weapons you choose and how you upgrade them to suit your own playstyle. There's not a more satisfying feeling than having a second encounter with an early game boss and absolutely destroying them after you've leveled up since your first encounter. There's so much variety in playstyle that is completely up to the player which keeps me coming back to multiple playthroughs with different playstyles and classes.
Dark Souls has some of the best level design I've ever seen in the game. Every location connects to another which connects to another which circles back to where you started. It really contributes to immersing you in what feels like a huge world with all sorts of different environments. You can easily get to any area in the entire game from the starting area which makes the game feel less tedious and mundane. For the most part, the environments look incredible and it's always exciting wandering into a new area, not knowing what new enemies and hazards could come next. Although one of the few things I dislike about this game is the environment of the early game, which feels somewhat samey and boring. However, once you get past that, the game opens up into interesting and dynamic landscapes and some of them have literally left me with my mouth wide open in awe (not even kidding my mind was blown).
I'll keep this section short because to be honest I haven't really dove very far into the world yet; but the lore for this game is fantastic and has so much behind it. The game doesn't force complex story down your throat and try to make you follow their narrative. You can pick up a good amount of very cool lore just through the world itself and interactions with NPCs. And if you are really captivated, then you can dig in deeper and find mind blowing stories behind characters and locations.
Is this game challenging? Yes. Will you die a lot? Yes. But don't let this game's reputation prevent you from experiencing a genuinely fun and well-designed game that stands as a landmark in the RPG genre.

I'd just like to get this out of the way: yes, I like Dark Souls. In fact, I love it. I think the only one I didn't outright love was 2, mostly due to the relatively bland enemy design when compared with the other games. Even 3 had monsters that would sprout out into horrific nightmare fuel abominations, but 2 was mostly knights in armor or standard humanoid figures with weapons. By this same reasoning, Bloodborne was probably my favorite, though it does lose points for not getting a PC port, something that would greatly fix the loading times.
So why don't I recommend this?
Because this port is sh!t. Like, impressively sh!t. Locks itself to 720p at 30fps and is basically unplayable with a mouse and keyboard, unleass you're the sort of person who rebinds every command to find the most optimal keys to lay commands before starting every game. Even with a controller, the framerate and the sheer number of graphical glitches I've experienced turned me off before getting through the first level. It's just simply unplayable.
Go buy it on console. Seriously. It's just a horrible port, but everything else is great. And while you're at it pick up all the other games as well. The learning curve's fairly steep, but it cements that feeling of accomplishment you get when you finally break through the barrier you've been up against for the last 3 hours.
EDIT: To those who may already own this game or are determined to get it working, I have had it pointed out to me that there is a mod called DSfix that can get it working. Having tried it out for a bit, I can say it does dramatically improve things, though you'll need some time, dedication, and a light-to-decent amount of tech literacy to get it working. Even then it has its issues; I'm searching now to see if there's anything else that would help. Still, while I recommend the console version still, if you are determined and can work with mods, feel free to work towards that. (Thank you to Wilserien for the information regarding DSfix.)

So often has Dark Souls been discussed, it's difficult to say anything new. If nothing else, I simply wish to add my voice to the chorus of well-deserved praises for the game.
What I will add is a couple of rebuttals to common criticisms. First, I found the Prepare to Die Edition port completely serviceable. It's nothing amazing, to be sure, but I found it perfectly playable unmodified with a USB controller. "Essential" mods like DSFix and PvP Watchdog are certainly worth exploring, but if you don't want to go to the trouble you can still absolutely enjoy the game.
Second (though this is well-known among the community), the game is not as absurdly difficult as it is often made out to be. If you're hesitant to try Dark Souls based on rumblings about how "insanely hard" it is, I encourage you to check it out. It's more that the game requires patience and perseverance to learn - moreso than many other games - than that it's unfair or excessively difficult. With willingness to apply yourself and search for tips on things you can't figure out yourself, I do believe anyone can get through this game. And really, the satisfaction of success, on top of the incredible lore, level design, and combat, make it all undoubtedly worthwhile.

Now that we are out of the way of my opinion; let us move onto the pros and cons.
PROS:
-There is potentially a hundred hours worth of gameplay which sums up to more hours worth of gameplay then a game like pokemon.
-It has a okay balance of making it super hard and then calming down in the peace phase
-It involves alot of strategy which gets you thinking
--Differing levels of Singleplayer difficulty (Easy, Normal, Hard, Impossible)
-Involves new aspects for tower defense like rotating range
-It makes fragile structures vital and adds more areas to defend
-The variety and differenciation between enemies has a good balance
-It has alot of achievements for achievement hunters
-It supports saving on steam cloud which some games do not
-They are constantly updating the game with around 3 patches a month
-It brings back the nostalgia of some amazing games you would've found on armor games around a decade ago
-The progression is dealt with well within the game
-Compared to alot of other indie games you get alot more dollar for your buck
-It can get quite addicting
-The game has many different modes
-It brings back the classic ages of time progression (Stone age, medieval age etc.) and puts it into a effective tower defense game
-It seems decently evident that there will be dlc in the future
-It has two amazing developers
-It involves a decent system of adjusting game speed
-You can manage units with ease
There is so much more to mention for the pros which is such a good thing. For the pros I'd give a 4/5
CONS:
-As mentioned above it is a very hardcore game which can turn people away from it
-It only has two developers unlike other popular titles with a full dev team
-There are very few hotkeys that have use
-You can select melee and ranged but you cannot select all at once besides the scrolling over the whole map to select all
-It can get very hard at times
-It has a ridiculous amount of microing and if you are not a hardcore gamer that can be really frustrating or boring

A very solid entry within the Nobunaga's Ambition series. It is a must have if you love KOEI strategy games. For someone who is new to these type of games, if you're tired of the same old game formula I'd recommend trying this game. Do not be fooled by the screenshots, the game's focus is not on the battles but on managing your castles, building fortresses, carving alliances and enemies, recruiting great (and not so great) generals to help lead your armies and manage your bases.
If you love the Sengoku period of Japan, you will absolutely love this game. The officers' bios while not extensively written, give infomation on even the most obscure general during this period. The game explains so many things about whats happening and why, there are cutscenes which are beautiful times, and also make you feel engaged in the history of this era. You can also recreate history by following the optional quests given to you to reenact historic battles such as the Battle of Sekigahara or the Battle of Okehazama. But fear not, you can also completely change history, want the Oda clan to perish under the Matsudaira? Go ahead. You can create your own officers and clans, there are scenarios you can choose to start from, either the Birth of Oda Nobunaga all the way up to The Battle of Sekigahara.
You can play as literally any faction, of course this is to be expected from KOEI's flagship strategy game Nobunaga's Ambition (and also Romance of The Three Kingdoms) unsatisfied? Just create your own faction and conquer Japan how you want to.
Gameplay is very typical for KOEI, so if you played past titles you know what to expect. For potential new players, the game is essentially a grand strategy but not exactly. People will liken it to Paradox titles and honestly they have nothing in common aside from a lackluster combat system. At first sight it may remind you of Shogun 2 due to the Steam Store screenshots but I assure you it is nothing like that as well aside from the era. Essentially the gameplay consists of starting off at a castle (or a fortress if you feel confident enough) and raise troops, grow crops, and collect/earn money. You assign officers as overseers of castles/forts and officers are the number one most important thing in this game as of any Koei strategy game. They dictate how strong your forces will be, some will be so great they can turn the tide of an overwhelming battle due to their sheer skills. You can forge alliances by sending officers to other clans and increasing their relationship points with you, once it hits a certain number you can send the offer and they will accept. You can request reinforcements depending on your relationship points with the clan, you can coordinate attacks with other clans and form coalitions against a huge clan to cut them down to size. You can vassalize other clans, form a lifelong alliance by sending marriage offers to other clans or if your daughters have good enough stats, keep them as officers. Construct new fortresses to increase your troop size even more. While it's not at the level of Paradox titles deep, it is very respectable and offers a NEW formula to strategy games.
The AI is extremely competent. A big thing in this game is you can only control so much of an area, once you conquer outside that area you need to move your capital or create a province for an AI general to control. You appoint a general to lead the province, give him officers and a few bases and he'll be good to go. The AI can grow their own playstyle and abilties as an overseer of a province. You can dictate who they attack, assist, and whether they transport spare resources. They do this on their own after you set the settings, however you can also force them to attack someone to coordinate a joint assault or defend a important base. If you set the dificulty settings high enough, you will be challenged by the enemy AI, they will attack you with large forces (if they are large enough) they will coordinate assaults on you with their allies, they will attempt to woo your officers into not fighting them or even worse, joining them.
Difficulty settings can be tweaked, Japanese voices are available (and recommended) The graphics, while not ultra-realistic or amazing in today's standards, are beautiful to behold and I found myself looking at the map and taking it all in, the officer portraits are also well done and it is easy to recognize someone from their portrait. I personally haven't had a crash yet in 55 hours of playing this game. I haven't ran into a major bug worth noting, If you were worried that KOEI may screw up the game because of their past ports you can feel at ease. KOEI has created strategy games and the Nobunaga's Ambition series in particular since 1983. This is their bread and butter, they have a formula and it works.
There will be complaints of the price point, complaints of DLC practices, and complaints how the game's battle system is lacking.
In regards to the price point, It is priced at a hefty $60. People who have never heard of this series will wonder why it costs so much and also read it is a "port" but further investigation will reveal that it is a TRANSLATION port of the game, the base game was made for PC in Japan. This version of the game also includes the PUK version of the Japanese game (which sold seperately in Japan) PUK stands for Power-Up-Kit, the equivalent of an expansion for the game.
The "day one DLC" issue many seem to have, as stated in the previous point, this is a translation of an already existing game. We should not expect to get the DLC for free that non-English customers paid for. You do not need the DLC, they simply add more scenarios.
And yes, the battle system is lacking as it always has in all KOEI strategy games. The game is essentially a grand strategy, there are very few tactics involved in these games. If you prefer a strong battle system, this game is not for you.
Many newcomers will ask themselves, if this game is so good, why havent I heard of it before? Well, KOEI had a policy of not exporting their RoTK/NA series to English speaking customers of the world for quite some time, they had released a few before, but they stopped for a while. This is the first time in a good amount of years they released Nobunaga's Ambition to western audience. This is also the first time they released the PUK edition to western audiences as well.
I can only hope that they will feel confident in the western market and continue to release english versions of their amazingly well done strategy games. They were sorely missed from this reviewer.

It's like Princess Maker and Black Box had a baby and wrapped it in a cutesy Machiavellian visual novel. You can go in blind or let it smack you with hints every now and then. Either way, take notes. LOTS of notes. Remember the Dwarf Fortress motto "Losing is Fun" and you'll do fine.

Everyone and everything is out to get you in Long Live the Queen. You play through this gorgeous visual novel as a young 14 year old princess whose mother has just recently passed away and you are thrust into tending to the everyday matters of running a kingdom. From going to parades, giving public speeches, being the judge jury and executioner in court cases, leading your nation to war or diplomatically resolving your international disputes. But such a young girl can’t just jump right in and successfully run a kingdom; she needs to be properly trained.
The game plays out on a week to week basis where you start off by choosing 2 school classes you would like to take to train your queenly skills, and with 42 different skills to level up there is plenty of depth and variables to take into account that makes each choice feel meaningful, If you just choose willy-nilly without putting thought into what to level up you will definitely wind up just like your mother. The skills are either negatively or positively affected by your princesses’ current mood, for example if you are overly willful you may earn bonus points for taking a course in naval strategy or internal affairs whereas if you were in a yielding mood you would have a penalty for naval strategy or internal affairs.
After monitoring your mood, and assessing which classes you want to take, and you’re skill points are distributed, you are then put into a dialogue scene where you are presented with various dialogue trees, events, and scenarios that either get passed or failed depending on whether or not you have trained enough in a certain skill, an example of this may be perhaps you are out in the courtyard and a snake crosses your path and strikes at you, if you have reached a high enough level in the “Reflexes” skill you will be able to react quick enough to avoid the attack and escape death. More often than not a crucial fail will result in your death, and that is where the game gets addicting, you keep wanting to go back and try to figure out what you did wrong and what you could have done differently to avoid your demise (most likely just to discover another way to die). The game is the equivalent of the anime version of Bill Murrays Groundhogs day, you’ll just keep reliving the same things over and over until you get it right, and quite frankly that style of game isn’t for everyone, it may become too repetitive for your liking or you may feel that you were cheated the way you died and you may become too frustrated to keep playing, but odds are that you’ll be back to try to live the 40 weeks to reach your coronation day and become queen.
The game offers plenty of interesting dialogue and has a beautiful art style; the art style paired with the brilliant piano sound track is truly an aesthetically pleasing combination.  The dark nature of the game is an overall exciting adventure experience and the high quality of both the visuals and especially the audio complement the game very well.

TL;DR: A great open world game with entertaining Arkham-inspired combat and a few other borrowed themes from games such as Assassin's Creed. Ultimately, the game wouldn't be nearly as great without the new (at the time) nemesis system, which will randomly generate unique nemeses who will remember their interactions with you, allowing you to create unique stories.
MINOR SPOILER ALERT - THIS REVIEW WILL CONTAIN MINOR SPOILERS, SO BE WARNED!
Graphics/Scenery
In my opinion the graphics are pretty good, although this is one of the most recent games I own, so compared to newer titles it may be rather poor.
The open world is nice to look at, after 300+ hours I have mostly memorized all of the various landmarks in the two large regions (one is unlocked halfway through the storyline). There is a fairly vast array of architecture/natural landscape, like rock outcroppings, cliffs, ruins being used as outposts, and massive strongholds with ziplines. Not to mention the regular orc models have a lot of variety.
Gameplay - Combat
The combat is based off of the Batman Arkham games (or so I've heard) and revolves around getting a high hit streak from striking opponents and parrying their attacks. Once your hit streak reaches a certain level, you can execute special moves such as fire arrows, instant executions, and ghostly wraith abilities.
I think the combat is good, it is still entertaining to play, especially when you are at lower levels and must utilize all of your abilities.
There are many different kinds of enemies to fight, including three beasts and five kinds of orcs (including the standard warrior). Each orc has certain advantages, and each one requires different tactics to defeat, from shield-bearing defenders, spear-throwing hunters, and dual-wielding berserkers each orc could potentially be your end.
Each nemesis has a unique set of combat abilities and weaknesses that can be discovered by gathering intel on them. Intel can be gathered by interrogating certain soldiers (called Worms), finding it on a dead body, or being seductively whispered into your ear by a freed slave. These sets of traits make the tactics used in fighting each nemesis different.
Gameplay - Progression
Progression in the game takes four forms; Power, Mirian, XP, and Runes.
Power is gained by killing orc Captains and Warchiefs, or by participating in Power Struggles such as Duels, Feasts, and Beast Hunts. Power is used to unlock Power Tiers, which allows you to purchase more powerful abilities.
XP is gained by killing enemies, liberating slaves, and even when you die. XP is used to unlock Ability Points which you spend to purchase more abilities. Some abilities are gained through the storyline.
Runes are gained by killing enemy Captains and Warchiefs. The level and type of the Rune depends on the strength of the orc, as well as the method you use to kill them. Utilizing an orc's fear or hate against it will increase the rune's level. Runes can be slotted into your sword, bow, and dagger (extra slots can be purchased with Mirian, maximum of five) and give unique benefits. There are dozens of different types of Runes, as well as Epic Runes which are much more rare than common Runes.
Mirian is an elven currency gained through completing side missions such as Sword, Bow, and Dagger Legends (which also increase the effectiveness of your weapons), grabbing collectibles, doing Hunting and Survival Challenges, and completing Outcast Rescue Missions (unlocked by rescuing outcast slaves, and usually involve rescuing slaves and killing their orc overlords.) Mirian can also be obtained by destroying duplicate/unwanted Runes. Mirian is used to increase your max health, ammunition, focus (slow down time in ranged mode), and can purchase powerful boons for your weapons (to unlock these boons I believe you must complete all of its legends).
Gameplay - Nemesis System
The nemesis system in this game is frankly quite amazing. While it has some limitations, there are hundreds of different kinds of orc captains and warchiefs, from butchers wearing aprons, to drunks who burp when they talk, and orcs with claws or peg legs.
Each nemesis will remember their interactions with you, including if they have killed you, if you have run away, or if you have exploited a weakness of theirs.
SPOILER ALERT BELOW:
some nemeses can even return from the dead baring scars and bandages
Gameplay - Other
Aside from this, I will briefly mention some other aspects of the game. First off, the stealth system is pretty good, with orcs having awareness meters that will appear if you enter their field of view, stealth kill animations, and orcs will investigate if they find corpses.
Second, there are countless opportunities in the environment that allows you to cause fear and terror amongst the orcs. These include:
- caged Caragors (great beasts)
- Morgai flies
- Bait to attract beasts
- weak portions of wall to collapse onto orcs
- Explosive barrels of alcohol (can also be poisoned)
+ more
Third, halfway through the game you unlock the ability to mind control orcs and create an army to challenge Sauron. This is insanely fun, as you choose whether to recruit an orc captain or slaughter him. It is incredibly awesome when a random orc defender you dominated helps you slay a Graug, and gets promoted to captain because of it (happened to me once).
Story
I personally like the story, although the boss fight at the end are very disappointing (you will be disappointed when you find out why) the midway boss was good, and the randomly generated warchiefs can be challenging at times as well. While the character development is very small (not nonexistent) there is a large cast of characters, including some familiar faces (my precious....) and comic relief in the form of a bumbling orc trying to rise through the ranks.
Verdict
Honestly this game is ridiculously fun, if you like the combat and Lord of the Rings (although major fans may be upset as it conflicts with canon) and are willing to have a bit of fun this game is guaranteed to have at least 15 hours of game time, although I would say the average person could easily get 100 hours. If it was the original price I would have reservations but I got it over a year ago on sale for 11 bucks and can easily say it is the best deal I have gotten in my life! Try it out now!

Overrated and boring to sum it up!
And to clarify: I don't hate the game by any means, i just can't approve it with all its flaws.
Starting of with what the game does right:
- The often praised orc ranking system has some great ideas and potential, which has not really been used in the end though
- Free flow combat system works as intended and is still very fun to use and rewards skillful use of its possible moveset
- World is designed to be able to go almost anywhere
- Parcour stuff works fine for the most part, but can also lead to some unwanted deaths if not working as desired
- Stealth missions feel well done, fair but still challenging, and are even more fun due to the free movement
- Lots of additional content from the GoTY edition offering more hours of gameplay
- Overall good amount of possible hours to play the game considering the price
- Middle-earth lore (for those who enjoy it)
And everything that makes it a bad game:
- Boring story with unlikeable characters and bad dialoque
- Even more annoying dwarf with even more annoying dialoque
- Unskipable orc intros, turning every fight into an orc speeddating sim
- Way too overpowered skills, game offering
no challenge, even when you blindly rush into every mob
- Side missions rather feel like a challenge mode rather than actual side missions
- Orc ranking system absolutely useless in the end
- Both areas boring, uninspired and empty
- Second half of the game recruiting your orc 'army' only leads to a 5 vs 5 fight with a few mobs
- Insultingly bad final boss fight only consisting of 5 QTEs
- Middle-earth lore (for those who dislike it)
What should make the game great and stand out (the ranking system) ends up being just a method to farm better runes, which is useless as the game is easy, long and repetitve enough even without farming, and to make fights against tougher enemies easier, which is also useless as you can easily pick up on them without any more help with your overpowered skillset.
Ends up being just a basic RPG with nothing that makes it worth being a AAA title or getting all the hype it got back when it was released.
Bought the game for 3,50€, so i don't feel cheated in any way. If you are really into that Middle-earth stuff, you can buy the game, if not you should only buy it, if it's on sale and if you got lots of free time and no other games to play.
Also be prepared to be disappointed.

Summary: This Portal 2 mod is of good quality, it brings a new interesting mechanic in along side the portal mechanic that we know and love, it brings a new and interesting spin in the world of the Portal universe, and it is entirely free as long as you have purchased Portal 2! However, the mod is not without it's faults, but ultimately, it is worth trying out, and in the end you have not payed for the experience.
The story begins from the end of Portal 2. You have just been released from Aperture Science, standing outside the shed placed in the middle of a vast field. But this is revealed to be a fake, as giant moniters displaying the outside world suddenly collapses. Visually it is an impressive display, but somehow the entire opening seems off, as barely any sound is played. Giant monitors coming crashing down at you in silence. This is a problem that happens repeatedly where som parts of the mod becomes a bit too quiet, but this mostly is confined to the beginning.
Following a path over the rubble, you will be placed in the very first test chamber, in the same style from Portal 1 and 2. These first chambers will be a tutorial at using the new time travel mechanic. The mod explains how it works and how to use it through monitors, displaying the chamber and what to do. The tutorials is very helpful at getting to know the mechanics, but a minor request for this is to make the key prompts on the screen bigger, it can be difficult to see what button needs to be pressed.
Once you are done with the tutorial, you will have to figure out the puzzles yourself, going from chamber to chamber, you will have to utilize both the time travel mechanic and your portal gun, to get things done. The time travel mechanic works by recording movements. Press "R" to start recording everything you do. Running, placing portals, picking up objects. Press "Q" to stop the recording. Press "F" to play back the recording, a clone of you will appear and redo everything you did in the recording. You will be using your clone for pressing buttons, to help you reach higher, and placing portals among more, making it feel like a co-op game you are playing alone. The mechanic is a welcomed addition, but it feels neglected at times.
Sometimes you will not even need to use it, which is a shame. Another thing is the usage of portals is very limited, it can only be used when the mod wants you to.
The mod introduces some new shiny white tiles, which can lead you to believe you can use your portal gun on them, but you can't. Only on special slightly darker white tiles can you use your gun, which created some confusion in the beginning. However, because the use of portals in this mod is very limited, I can see the need for this "Non-Portal" white tiles, otherwise the chambers would be way too dark.
The mod takes a detour from the usual chamber after chamber with a few story elements, revealing bits and pieces of what has happened, but leaving a lot of things for you to think about. The story itself is short. So is the mod. Completing it will take about 1 to 2 hours, and the end does not offer a conclusion, it ends with more questions than answers, definately sets the scene for a sequal / future updates.
The difficulty level in this mod seems to be a bit off. One peticulary chamber was a quite tricky puzzle to solve, but the next chamber offered no difficulty whatsoever. It happens a few times where the difficulty just flies all over the place, but it is not something that destroys the experience.
There is many reports on bugs and crashes. I have personally not found any bugs in the mod, and I have only experienced a single crash during the end credits. Be prepared for some technical issues along the way.
This mod is in no way without faults. It is a bit too short, the ending coming abruptly when you think the story is about to really kick off. There appears to be some sound issues / some sounds missing. The mechanics is at times not fully utilized, several reports on bugs, and the difficulty does what it pleases. But none of this is enough to ruin the experience. Thinking with Time Machine is for the most part a high quality mod, bringing in a new fun and interesting mechanic that fits the original game. It has an interesting spin on the lore of Portal (If one such thing exists). And the puzzles in the game can be difficult, but never unfair. Overall this mod is worth your time, you can spend a couple of hours on it and have fun. So let's hope the team behind it adds more to it. Adding a level editor similar to Portal 2 can help make this mod more long lasting. If you already have Portal 2, you should try it out. Afterall it is free.

Alright, so I've been playing Miscreated for 368.6 hours and am finally ready to deliver my review on this game. I had VERY high hopes for it but, in the end, I must give Miscreated a 2 out of 5 stars.
Pros:
First off, the game looks absoutely stunning. Alot of patience and dedication have been put into the models, character models could still use a bit of work and maybe some customization options. But the landscape is gorgeous, the rain effects are the best I've ever seen and the fog is creepy as balls. The weapons could do with a bit of wear on them, right now they all look pristine and new, clothing too. All of the clothing looks like it just came out of the factory. Don't get me wrong, the clothing looks amazing. But it looks new and this is supposed to be several years after a nuclear war. Clothing wouldn't be pristine after it's been laying on the ground for a few years.
Secondly, the weapons deal believable damage. Aside from the Brute, any mutant/zombie will die from 1 shot to the head or 3 to the chest. The Brute is the exception, regardless of your weapon, it's going to take multiple shots to the head. The M16 takes 5 headshots, pistols I don't know. Wasn't gonna try. But the M40A1, the most powerful weapon in the game, takes atleast 3 headshots. I say atleast 3 because I was only able to get 2 in him before he got too close for comfort and I switched to the M16.
Third, if you die, don't panic. Corpse despawn time was recently increased to 20 minutes. So, as long as you avoid zombies and just keep running, you will be able to get back to your coprse. Last time I died I was in Hayward, up at the very top of the map and respawn down in the Amalgamated Airfield which is all the way at the bottom of the map. I was able to get back to my corpse but it despawned only 15 seconds after my arrival.
Cons:
First con, and the most annoying to me, bugs that do not cause the game to crash are most likely not going to be addressed. Yet at the same time, a bug no one even noticed or cared about will be. For example, the Devs recently modified the laser sight to be less visible, but yet when you're driving a vehicle and hit a mutant or even a bump in the road your vehicle will go airborn and likely flip and explode. A problem that has existed before I started playing and still has not been addressed. If a vehicle is not moving fast enough it will not deal damage to mutants. Anyone ever had their foot ran over by a slow moving tractor? Ouch. That mess deals damage Devs, trust me.
Second, no snap points and silly build restrictions. The Devs have decided not to install snap points for base building so as to promote "creative freedom", yet have also decided that you can't build any higher than like 9 meters or so. So your base is going to be very short. Me, I love to build big. Towers, fortresses, I could tolerate the convoluted and complex mess that is base building in this game if I had REAL creative freedom. You even have a limit to how wide your base can be. First off, and this is REALLY Fing dumb, you have to set a plot sign that claims a certain spot as yours and sets up your build perimeter. Now I do agree that some invisible magic force needs to prevent other players from building on your base. RUST has this problem. You log off and some yayhoo killed you, because your body doesn't despawn when you log off and walled up the insides of your base so now it's useless to you. But the plot sign is just the dumbest of things, not to mention it looks tacky as hell sitting in the middle of your base. A better way to handle this would have been to set each base piece to expand the magic field a little, this way people could build as big as they want but yayhoos still can't troll them by Fing up their base. Also, there's a 240 piece limit. Your base can only consist of 240 pieces... Really? Atleast on private servers, like mine, this should be able to be turned off to give players real freedom.
Third, and the most hated con, storage limit. The Devs have decided that you're only allowed to make 1 large and 1 small storage box. And neither offers a decent storage amount. You can find tents out in the world, but they don't offer much space either and the server will only allow 10 tents for the entire server. Keep in mind a server is atleast 36 player slots and tents can be hard to find. There's also vehicle storage, but the luggage cart and farm tractor, 2 vehicles that don't even have trunks or anything, have the same storage capacity as a bus or 5 ton cargo truck... What are these Devs smoking? Aside from the fact that hording supplies like food and drinks and such is the most basic of basics of survival, I love collecting weapons and clothing in these games so I can change it up from time to time. But with such limited storage capacity that's just not possible. Now, I do have a back up of my current weapons and clothes, which takes up most of my storage, but I do have most of the weapons, each with a full clip. But since my storage is already full my base is in a store where food spawns a plenty, that's... convenient. But I can only take my collected weapons out JUST around my base as I can't store enough spare ammo for them to actually explore with them. My mains are the M16 and Renegade, so I have spare piles of ammo for them. And ammo stacking is a whole nother can of worms, especially for the revolver. Some genius Dev decided that .357 rounds can only be stacked in stacks of up to 6 rounds... Now you're just Fing with me guys. But most other ammo can only stack up to piles of 10 to 30 rounds, so your puny inventory can quickly fill up with ammo, especially if you have a real survival mindset and grab any ammo you see. I've actually gotten to the point where I have to walk past ammo, even for my mains, because it spawns so abundantly.
Which brings me to my 4th problem. This is a survival game right? Then why does everything spawn so abundantly? Thristy? Hungry? Then stop running past houses. Every single one of them will have enough food and water for you to grab some extra. Low on ammo? Then quit shooting inanimate objects. If you use your ammo with a survival mindset of making every shot count then you'll end up with mountains of ammo. Especially considering the fact that there are very few mutants in the game. PvP servers are going to be your only real challenge for maintaining ammo... if you're a total newbie to FPS or tend to panic and spray and pray. Hunting is a thing in this game... no body really bothers as food is just SO readily available in literally every house. To be perfectly honest, the only SURVIVAL aspect of this game is zombies and player douches. My server is PvE, with PvP being only during special events. So the game just doesn't feel like a survival game at all. It's a... poorly assembled base building game that looks good but doesn't function well at all.
So now you're probably wondering: "Gee Stahl, if there's so much wrong with the game, why did you play for almost 400 hours?" And the answer is simple, I hit it off with some folks right off the bat and been playing with them constantly. But I also, again, had really high hopes for this one. This game looks AMAZING, I tip my hat to the artists. And the Devs do communicate with players on their discord channel. Though I've come to see that there is only a small number of players they will actually respond to. This Hendrik fellow is the only Dev I've actually seen talking and I have tried to make suggestions for the game, even mentioning him directly as some players have. But neither he, nor any other Dev, has ever responded to me, leading me to believe that players have to, somehow, buy the Devs attention.
It's for these reasons that I really just can't recommend Miscreated. The game has SO much potential, but it is wasted by an incompetent Dev team. They have the skill and know how to make this game everything it could be but just won't. (review length limit reached)

In full disclosure I will admit that the only other Ace Combat game I have played is AC04:Shattered Skies, AC04 is one of my favorite games with an excellent combination of good story telling and solid controls, as such I am going to be using it as my reference point and I expect the majority of the other titles in the series to follow in AC04's vein. I will also admit that I have not played much of ACAH due to its multitude of problems, which include the issue of controls and the radical shift in game play compared to AC04.
The controls are awkward to players use to the traditional combination of mouse and keyboard flight simulators, they involve a combination of the arrow keys for the place of a joystick and place the yaw and acceleration on to the wasd. This setup does not give the precision that a mouse and keyboard or a controller gives, it just feels really clunky. Though the control settings claim to support mouse and keyboard, that is only during the helicopter and rail gun segments, the mouse is not supported when piloting fixed wing aircraft. This is a serious problem when you consider the fact that the game focuses on close range arcade style dogfighting, something that inherently requires precision, and leads to frustration at overturning your opponent almost constantly.
The gameplay itself is solid, if this had not been an ace combat game I may even call it good, it involves closing behind the opponents aircraft, pushing a button, and entering a “dogfight mode” where the camera is zoomed in and your reticule is expanded. In the dogfight mode the opponent is locked to your speed and can only turn, the goal is to use your cannon or a well timed missile to knock out your opponent. But my real issue is the fact that the gameplay is just so different from AC04 that it feels like a completely different series, it feels more arcady and badly put together. The controls don't help the game in anyway, so you really should buy a controller or a supported joystick (of which there are few) before purchasing the game.
TL;DR: Controls are clunky and require a controller or joystick to use, the gameplay is so radically different that it might as well be a game from another series. A good game, but not a good Ace Combat.

Do you like survival games, but are sick of gathering materials for crafting by punching the same boring trees and mining the same boring cobblestone and doing little else as a generic nameless survivor ?
Well, in this game once you create your own character out of the SEVEN PLAYABLE SPACE FARING SPECIES (which each have their own ship, racial armor, weapons, dialogs and cosmetic features you can chose from), you CAN (and will, because frankly you have better things to do than mining your brains out) progress through the game ONLY by exploring varied dungeons, labs, villages and stations, populated by (sometimes) friendly NPCs that will provide you with quests, trading opportunities and sometimes even ask to join your crew !
Progression is also deeper than most games in its category as you will go through 8 TIERS of various armors and randomly generated ranged AND melee weaponry, with differents stats, looks, handling and effects.
You found a sick armor with amazing stats, but it looks like a power-ranger armor and you're allergic to the color pink ?
Fear not ! You can dye ANY piece of armor you find to suit your needs. Not enough customisation ?
Why not put ANOTHER armor piece in the cosmetic slot and dye THAT one to achieve the look of your dreams ?
You finally look fantastic, but your ship looks like a flying trash bin and is also the size of a trashbin ?
Why not upgrade it into a mobile penthouse, deck it out in decoration and throw parties with your 12 crew members AND other players ?
If you found musical instruments on your travels, you can even play music together from a tracklist expendable through the steam workshop !
And when you've had enough fun playing around, save the galaxy from unspeakable tentacley evil in story missions concluded by bossfights which have no business being this good in a survival game !
And once THAT's done...well.
Why not do it all over again with a new character ?
That sound stupid, you say ?
Maybe...but that's how i netted my ridiculous playtime, and i still discover new things every playthrough.

This game wasn't quite what I expected from the descriptions on the store page, but I enjoyed it anyways.  It's not perfect but it is enjoyable.  And at times quite challenging.  This game is about surviving, not killing all the zombies.  You must scavenge for supplies, and help out survivors in need, often times bringing them home to join your group.  The zombies respawn regularly, and at times seem like they come out of nowhere to attack you.  If you die, you are dead forever and must switch to one of your other companions.  The map is large, but it is the only map you get to play without the Lifeline expansion/dlc pack.  I found the controls to be a bit weak, and all of the characters seem to be pretty much the same to me.  They might have a special skill like cooking for medicine that is useful to your group, but as far as playing as them, they all seem about the same to me.  The store page says you can design your base, which isn't really true.  You pick a base on the map and move to it, then you simply choose what kind of rooms it will have, such as an infirmary or workshop.  Not really much customization in that area.  The one thing about this game that I really didn't like was that they released the dlc packs while the game was still early access.  The Breakdown DLC is simply a different game mode on the same map as the main game.  It should have been included with the main game.  The other dlc, Lifeline, is on a new map thankfully, but it seems small.  The gameplay is slightly different in that one, but not enough for me to warrant a dlc.  I pretty much felt like I was paying for a new map.  With that said, the DLCs are must haves if you enjoy the game, as the main game will likely leave you wanting more if you enjoy it.  Overall it is a fun game, and a challenging one.

Secara kesuluruhan, itulah yang lo bakalan lakukan ketikan bermain game ini. Lo secara gak langsung diwajibkan untuk masuk dari rumah ke rumah untuk mencari makanan, obat, senjata, amunisi, minyak, dan bahan bangunan. Begitu lo udah dapat salah satu suply, lo bisa tampung itu ke dalam mobil dan cari lagi ke rumah atau bangunan lainnya. Tentu saja, gak semudah itu. Selalu ada zombie disetiap lo berada, BAHKAN ketika lo ada di markas. Btw zombie nya ini bener bener sensitif banget sama suara lo. Suara mobil, pistol, senjata, bahkan ketika lo sedang loot dirumah. zombie nya bakalan datang. Daaaaann... gak cuman itu aja... ada berbagai macam zombie, ada yang Big Un, Feral, dan SWAT zombie. Mamam dah tuh... eh maksudnya lo yang dimamam zombie. Setelah lo loot, lo juga bakalan crafting. Tapi ini craftingnya sederhana banget, lo cuman crafting kaya ammo, mine, dsj. Disisi lain lo bisa juga merancang markas lo sesuai dengan kebutuhan lo menggunakan hasil loot. Singkat kata, lo bisa membangun basecamp pertahanan diri.
Lifeline: nanti bakalan ditulis lagi
Breakdown : sama...
Lo adalah karakter random yang sedang berlibur disebuah pegunungan dan tau tau diserang oleh zombie. Begitu lo diserang, lo berusaha mencari informasi ke pos gunung terdekat. Sayangnya pos gunung itu juga sedang diserang zombie. Lo, temen lo, dan penghuni pos mempertahan pos tersebut. Tapi sayangnya, salah satu dari anggota pos tersebut mati. Lo pun mendengar dari radio bahwa terdapat suatu komunitas yang mempertahankan diri di gereja. Lo dan teman lo kesana berusaha mencari tempat berteduh dan pengobatan. Satu hal yang gue sesalkan selain grafik dari game ini adalah tidak ada cutscene yang indah. Semuanya ya sama aja... konfilk yang terjadi didalam game sudah bagus tapi... pembawaanya kurang emosional. Berasa banget kakunya.
Secara keseluruhan, game ini pantas banget untuk mengisi hari hari lo. Walau pun terdengar sederhana, selalu ada perasaan menantang, menghibur, dan wow banget ketika lo looting, bertahan hidup, dan membangun markas lo sendiri. Btw game ini single player yaa.. jadi lo gak perlu khawatir, lo gak bakalan ketemu orang yang nge-troll lo. Lo bener bener bisa fokus membangun komunitas yang harmonis ditengah dunia yang busuk. Satu hal lagi, game ini berjalan sesuai waktu realtime, artinya kalau di ingame ada tulisan waktu 30menit, maka lo harus menunggu waktu 30menit di reallife. Disamping itu, lo 'dipaksa' untuk terus bermain game ini atau uninstall. kenapa? karena kalau lo tinggalkan begitu aja, komunitas lo bakalan MATI walau pun lo gak mainin. Ingat dengan game tamagochi? Nah... State Of Decay adalah game dimana lo harus merawat komunitas lo layaknya Tamagochi.

A fantastic tower defense game. When compared to Dungeon Defenders the gameplay is far more satisfying and fun, though it comes with it's own downsides such as being limited to only 2 players at a time.
In DD you end up just min-maxing the DPS of your turrets and the game boils down to boring stats and meta play, but this game is far more casual and focused on simpler, more satisfying gameplay that doesn't sacrifice difficulty.
Mob control is not about simply doing a ton of damage (though it still and your usual gamut of slowing, freezing, burning effects etc) but adds the element of displacing them into off-track hazards, knocking them down or out with pushers, launch pads and haymakers. Nothing is more satisfying then knocking a group of mobs down a flight of stairs with a giant swinging spiked wall trap.
Again, the 2 player max thing is a big downside, and running decreases your FOV which can get annoying and make it seem like you aren't going any faster.
Still, there is not a ton of grinding necessary in this game to unlock new gear like there is in similar games. The levels are well built, and the selection is decent. There is no lack of challenge either. I have not bothered to attempt nightmare difficult on any map because I get steamrolled every time. I would like to see more content, but perhaps they're just working on OMD 3 now.
Definitely play this with a friend.

This is a simple game.  A game that you will play after a long day of taking a beating from your boss that happens to have a god-complex.  A game that will make you wish you played more of the retro-style games when you were younger.  A game that will find you staring at your screen in awe as you discover that your defense was meaningless!  On a serious note, though, this game is epic.
PROS:
-Sexy retro graphics
-A slight twist (and improvement) on the traditional TD style
-Replayability is quite ok (for its money's worth)
-Differing levels of Singleplayer difficulty (Easy, Normal, Hard, Impossible)
-1 vs 1 casual multiplayer battles in a sort of Warcraft III custom map feel
-Minimal bugs, maybe 2 or 3 tops
-An active developer
CONS: (I understand this is a newborn game)
-A slightly complicated UI, and this might make beginners feel rather overwhelmed (you get used to it after about 15 minutes, though)
-The multiplayer community is in dire need of players
-A somewhat linear style of gameplay, and players may find themselves undergoing a repetitive cycle if they aren't enthusiastic about TD
SUMMARY:
-A great concept, nice gameplay, nostalgia-inducing.  I feel like this game will grow well if the developer continues to work on this, and doesn't leave it dead.  A LOT of potential for tons of updates in the future and exciting content.  I say, give this game a shot guys.

I didn't know what I was getting into with this one. After reading reviews, testimonials, everything about the game it describes how you will die by chocolate. I did not die by chocolate on my first five tries even once... I did have a number of other grisly fates however.
Those fates are primarily the crux of the game, the idea that there are plenty of ways to get killed as a monarch, and you must survive them all for your dynasty to continue. From looking at reviews, and achievements, there appears to be innumerable ways the story can permeate, which leads to a lot of replayability. Even in my few hours I was able to notice major differences in the story... as well as consistencies. As nice as a diverging main plot is, it doesnt seem very diverging. All five tries had the same main plot driving the game forward, same series of major events. Maybe it was just my choice of side events, but I didnt see anything personally which led me to believe these were my choices. Even when i tried to diverge, i ended up with the same main plot. Maybe once i sink my hours in I will see more content.
The content I did see was very well done. Nice pictures, backgrounds, emotes, and music all add to the experiance greatly, giving an emotional depth to it. Of course, its not a tightly story driven "visual novel" (which is a term I personally reserve for romantic or eroge styles of the genre, LLtQ is a game pure and simple, not an interactive novel), but it still is able to make you see the lore and story of the universe, showing the intense effort put into crafting this world. Everything about the game resounds quality, and in such a small and concise package. Simple, elegant, yet deep and complex, and resounding with feeling from every ounce.
This intense feeling gave me chills even. The idea of playing a "king simulator" or in this case "queen simulator" is a very intriguing game type that highly interests me. The idea of being so vulnerable, but having that power still is something that I really want to like and play with, but I always hate being assassinated. But with this game at least assassions means you start all over and can make better choices, unlike some other king games where you just might end up in a worse mess than before *looks at crusader kings 2*. Either way, the tense edge-of-your-seat feeling the game gave me, as well as the feeling of power when I -spoiler warning- disintegrated a thousand peasents in a second with a fireball, was really satisfying.
The game has no major issues from what ive seen, other than maybe no "randomised" plot but thats just a personal want from me. So I would recommend the game if you like king games and can stomach the kawaii desu desu aesthetic.

So i just finished this game (14Hours) and OOOFFF where to start? I played it really careful, so tried to speak with every NPC and so on.
If you like Storytelling RPGs this game is for you. I would put it under the Undertale Genre, even theres no fighting element in it.
The Game plays in an Anthro Universe, with Animal-Human-likes. You play as Mae, a cat that dropped out of college and got back to her Hometown, Possum Springs, to life by her parents again. You meet old friends of Mae and must decide with which of them you want to hang out. This alternates your Main Story and the ending you get. Often you get to decide what you want to answer, too. The beginning is a bit slow but then the Story gets so WEIRD and FREAKY i love it! It got so immersive, all i want from such type of game.
You also have some build-in Minigames to loosen the only-chat gameplay, theyre well done and i really enjoyed them.
Now some Pro and Contras:
Pro:
-Fantastic Story, freaky, spooky, immersive, just perfect!
-Very well written dialouge, like for real

-Epic Soundtrack
-loveable Characters.

Contra:

End Conclusion:

If you're a great fan of Romance of the Three Kingdoms and or have great interest in anciente japanese history, this game is for you!
KOEI is already very famous because of Samurai Warriors, Dynasty Warrior and Warriors Orochi series, but few people do know about their great titles from Historical Simulations series like Romance of the Three Kingdoms (RoTK) and Nobubaga's Ambition (NA).
In this case, NA: Sphere of Influence tells the japanese history from the ascencion of the Oda Clan until japanese unification by Tokugawa. During the game you need to balance your actions in political, domestics and militaristics question, not forgetting to tell about all the others problems that may appear like, for example, treasons.
You have two options during the game, you can follow the hisical flow, learning a little more from the japanese history while repeating the same steps and decisions from the leaders from the time or if you want you can play everything on the fictional way of the history, trying to conquer and unify Japan under the flag from the clan that you choose or even in a clan that you have created.
One of the biggest problems from this game compared to others from the hitorical simulations is that, at least for me, this title is a lot easier if compared with RoTK, wherer I have played it since the SNES version and found more difficult in the IX, X and XI game from the serie, where you needed to do a better control and balance between the militaristic/diplomatic aspects of the game and needed to think a lot more in the combats where the weapon, general and skills available played a more important role in all the aspects of the game.
Finally, to finish this brief review, if you like a game with all these  aspects allied with some strategy during the combats (that you can choose to fight your battles or only wait for a result) this game is for you. If not, stay away from the game and don't waste your money. If you want a better opinion, take a look on YouTube for gameplay videos and see for yourself.

This game is really fun. If you like turn-based strategy, you'll like this game. It has elements of Civ, Total War, Crusader Kings, and similar games but there are some unique challenges. The game was complex - and not necessarily intuitive or documented - but almost everything could be automated if you prefer.
Managing your officers is really fun and you have plenty of time to develop favorites among the many unique characters working for you. Diplomacy is also essential. There are many competing clans and if you go to war you'll need to have truces, if not alliances, with your other neighbors. Don't give a neutral neighbor an opportunity to attack you while you're otherwise tied up as they will take it.
The only downside, if you want to call it that, is the same-ness of the map. Over the years I've played plenty of strategy games that take place in Japan, and I quickly was slightly irritated that the map was so predictable. Don't get me wrong, it's very well done in this game. There are tons of strategic choke points, benefits to plains vs mountains, and so forth. I kept having flashbacks to Shogun 2 as I played and tbh Shogun 2 did have a prettier (and more interesting) world map.
This game is great. I doubt it will be anywhere near as popular with Western audiences as it should be. And that's too bad because I'd love to see a modern Romance of the Three Kingdoms in English. If this doesn't do well it's unlikely they'll bring that title over.

This is one of the best mods of Portal 2 out there. The added time travel self co-op mechanic works PERFECTLY with the portal mechanics and gives a new and refreshing twist on the portal experience. So if you have portal 2 you should totally get this!
NOW FOR THE FLAWS:
This game is buggy as HELL and if you end up crashing every 2 seconds check out the game's forums for help. As for flaws in the actual game, there are two areas I want to talk about; the story and the level design.
The story starts off in a very clever way following up after the events of portal 2 to the second that game ended. This opening segment is executed very well and sets the mood perfectly. There are only two more instances of story in the whole game and they are not pulled off nearly as well. The only one that has substance which you encounter early in the game sets up a lot of things that never really get followed up later on which makes me wonder why were they even included in the first place. The ending is rather clever as well for how it ties into portal 2 and the game's time travel mechanic but it was a rather abrupt end that left me confused. It had no build up to it or real substance so it felt like the story ended just as it was getting started. However, you don't play this game for the story, you play it for the portal puzzles.
The level design for the most part is pretty solid and a joy to figure out their solutions--except for two puzzles which are completely broken. Chamber 5 and chamber 7 have glaring flaws in their design that seem rather hard to miss on the developers end. In chamer 5 you can permanently stuck in not just one area of the map, but TWO, and you'll have no choice but to manually restart the level. Rather silly and ruined an otherwise good puzzle. Chamber 7 is completely broken since you can bipass the real puzzle rather easily and this method of beating the puzzle is actually more obvious than the real puzzle. I did go back and try the real puzzle in the way the game intended me to and its a pretty darn good puzzle. Shame its deemed unnecessary by an oversight in its design.
Other than that this game was very enjoyable and you should totally pick it up and play it.

TL;DR: Really nice game to fair price. If you like RTS/Tower Defense and have someone to play it with in multiplayer buy it immediatly!
I followed the development of this game for a while and bought it on release and I wouldn't say I'm disappointed, no it's definitely a really nice game. I'm a huge fan of indie games and also of RTS games, so this game was an easy buy-choice for  me. And I don't regret the purchase, but this game is still not perfect. There are many small things that bug me and some of them are easily fixable. And I hope this game gets more content in future updates.
The biggest thing everyone who buys this game will notice immediatly is that this game has no resolution option at all, which would be no problem if it was in HD anyway or would have pixelart style, but its more in a flash-game kind of style, i.e. it has sort of high resolution textures and tries to look "realistic". I like the design and it fits the game perfectly but because there is no resolution option the game will be noticable blurry (at least in the main menu) when played in fullscreen. But I can live with that.
Then there is the 30 fps lock, which really is no problem at all because of the gameplay. But I noticed that when you advance time at night the fps lock will switch to 60, 90 and 120 fps, which then speeds up the game. That's not really professional, but it works...I guess.....nice workaround...but this probably explains why it has a 30 fps lock instead of 60 fps. Since 4x60fps = 240fps which would probably cause some problems on less powerful systems.
Next thing that I noticed are some AI problems here and there. The AI really has no AI at all except maybe some kind of pathfinding. This kinda sucks because you'll always have to rotate your troops so that they attack the enemy. You can't set something like patrol paths or auto-rotation. And everytime you change the direction of your ranged units you'll have to change it back, because the position-saving only saves their position, and not their rotation, so when you say them to go back to their default position but you rotated them earliert they will then look in the wrong direction. Dev, pls fix this!
Then there is the problem that most of the times you won't find someone to play with, and I doubt this will change in the future, probably it will become even harder. But yea, that's because not enough people play this game, that's not the games fault :D

My review may be biased by the year I waited craving to play this game that was a console exclusive but I guess it's fine...
Anyways, the game is a gem: extremely good mechanics, extremely good graphics, extremely good music, various and interesting "game" modes, unlockables, actually working netplay.
Now, in detail. Guilty Gear Xrd mechanics are probably "weaker" than Guilty Gear XX^core+R but still on a top tier level, they gave more freedom on Roman Cancels use and found a good way to make them netplay-viable, most old mechanics like Faultless Defence, Gatling Combos and Instant Kills are still there just like they were on previous titles and overall they feel extremely solid.
Game artwork/graphic is amazing. You play full-fledged 3D models and you almost can't tell they actually are 3D models instead of hand-drawn sprites until the camera pans/zooms for special events... amazing.
As always character design is flawless, animations are good (anime-styled deformations and such included) and generally speaking, the tech/workflow behind such an amazing result is most likely going to be used as example in the future by developers.
Music is good, yep. Ishiwatari Daisuke strikes again.
Now, about game modes. You think you're buying a fighting game, but you actually buy a fighting game, an in-game graphic animated visual novel/anime and a nice fighting RPG (M.O.M. mode), not to mention the Bonus Soundtrack (which is not Guilty Gear Xrd Soundtrack, it's a Bonus Sountrack for real).
Finally, netcode. I can't say the netcode has no issues, but I was able to play smooth matches with friends I know I ping good against. For fighting games netcodes are almost always "the hard test", mostly because it's the one thing you can't beta test enough and that tends to change a lot moving from different consoles or PC.
So, well, it's not that bad, not that good either, definitely playable on a good level if both players have a good ping.
Recommended? Yes, yes and yes again, one of the few games you cannot regret spending money for.

A true flawed game.  Whilst there are technical hitches, personally these are mostly AI based, the concept and atmosphere of the game itself is solid.  Indeed, it could be said that the world itself, a large valley in small-town America, is the real star of the show:  The world feels authentic and lived-in, with Marie-Celeste-like scenes playing out in the myriad houses, shops and industrial sites that can be scavenged.  The levelling mechanics, whilst simple, help to make each character distinct, and the loss of a highly skilled marksman or doctor can seriously impact the group's survivability.  Character death is permanent:  There are no essential characters, even those with story-relevant content are fair-game, adding to the general tension when leaving your home base.  Whilst the home base mechanics are simple, there is enough variety to aim for a variety of builds with a range of different abilities (why a dining area costs the same amount of resources as a munitions lab, however, eludes me).
Overall an extremely fun game, I recommend that you also pick up the Breakdown and Lifeline dlcs for sandbox mode and an alternate storyline from an "Antagonistic" perspective.

As someone who was just a wee lad playing on his NES when the first Nobunaga's Ambition hit the US, I was definitely turned on when they announced the 30th anniversary edition. The story of the Warring States Period is a crazy part of world history, not just Japanese history, and SOI adds infinitely more flair and backstory to this than previous editions of the game.
The game's combat has some similar elements to Total War: Shogun, but there's more art to it and fewer technical options available for directing your armies... The personalities in this game are more important, and your generals and their special talents can make or break you in a tough situation. The game has stronger RPG elements in developing their individual traits that can turn them into some serious powerhouses on the battlefield.
Enemy AI is pretty tenacious. They'll do a good job of trying to outmaneuver you on and off of the battlefield, and will definitely pounce on you in a weak moment. I was also impressed that it showed the same wariness in defending itself... For several years I was allied with one major clan, and they continued to plow through neighbors as if I might as well have been a wall or an ocean at their backs. As soon as I dissolved the alliance, their aggressive behavior came to a sudden halt. Turned out they were building up to take revenge on me, which they did. /restart
The building/management side of the game is very detailed. While there are only a few core resources you're trying to accumulate, there are multiple routes to the same destination, so skillful use of your generals and placement of buildings can really add up over time. As your clan gets bigger and bigger, there are options for delegating responsibility to the AI; take advantage of this because, otherwise, the game can start to feel a bit tedious and clunky.
Diplomacy's pretty simple and straightforward, and not to be underestimated in its usefulness. I'd like more options such as being able to request or hand over territory, but it was still enough to get the job done.
Historical quests are presented as optional objectives in the game, so that you can learn the stories of the major players in the Warring States Period. If you are unfamiliar with the period, are a fan of visual novels, and/or just want the free perks rewarded for finishing them, they're a nice little bonus.
I do miss the ninjas. In previous versions you could stab your rivals and sabotage their lands, etc... Something special about an 8-bit katana putting an end to your foes without a single soldier ever taking the field.
My one bit of advice in playing the game would be... click on All The Things. The tutorial is there but it misses so much. Information is available but you generally have to go looking for it, i.e. click on every item for the first time so that its associated Help page pops up to explain things. There were some features I didn't know existed until later in the game, that I would've prefered to know about from the get-go. This was particularly the case with delegating parts of my empire like I mentioned earlier, and I saw a couple of reviews that complained about the burden of management because they probably didn't know about this stuff either. Just click everything now and thank me later.
And on that note, I just united Japan so I'm finally ready to decompress.

This game is good. Just a simple Tower-Defense/RTS hybrid in the same vein as some zombie survival flash games you might've seen on Armor Games about a decade ago. Like those games, this one has a very addicting nature and you'll find yourself sinking a good number of hours into the Arcade mode, trying to get further and further every time. So far my best playthrough is 22 waves.
Fortify plays in a very simple manner. You have a fort that starts out very low tier with just a couple of slingshooters to hold back the tides of evil. As you gain more gold, you'll unlock new units. You'll upgrade your fort and build outposts which produce 1 of 3 resources that are used to further upgrade your fort. You'll progress through three tech levels; Iron Age, Medieval Age and Imperial Age. Starting from slingshots and ending with rifles and grenades. Aside from the 2 campaigns in the game (Northern, West) you also have an endless Arcade mode and a multiplayer mode where you can battle against 1 other player.
In summation, a very solid title that I've had an absolute blast with. And for 4.99, you can hardly beat it! A lot of indie titles price themselves out of the market, assuming they have plenty of content for the price. This title can actually carry that boast.

I finished this game and I enjoyed myself.  Here's why:
* Arcade style gameplay.  I wasn't looking for a simulator, and this game allowed me to learn to play quickly.
* Pick-up-and-play.  Menus weren't a pain to navigate, missions lasted long enough to feel satisfying, but not so long that they interfered with the other things I have to do in life.
* Good graphics. They're not 4k graphics, but the game does look great with it's combination of textures and lighting.
* HUD and UI. The targeting system was good. You can identify enemies, you can spot allies. I don't know if there's a colorblind mode though.
* When you get close to certain targets while dogfighting, the game will switch into a fast paced chase mode. It's really fun, but there's a small learning curve.  I thought it made the game more cinematic while still keeping gameplay intact.
* I enjoyed the story. I'm sure there are points against it, but I'm glad the story didn't take itself too seriously while still retaining the drama.
* Multiple airplanes, including helicopters. Helicopters flew well. Some planes steered like cows.
* Scaling difficulty.  Lots of easy stuff so you feel like a badass, but the game requires more and more skill from the player as the story continues.
Like any game, there are some bugs and glitches.

Wow. I couldn't not review this masterpiece.
This game has feels throughout the entire story. It gives you a feeling of wanting to fix petty things at first, but adds deeper elements to the characters and the town you interact with as you get connected to the whole expereince. It has a slow beginning that allows you to adjust to Mae's routine, but fills the world around you with open-ended and relatable problems lying around. The plot follows a similar pattern by leaving burning questions unanswered until a very intense ending sequence that left me absolutely stunned.
The mysterious story and characters are definitely the highlight of the game, but the main reason I was drawn to this game was the beautiful atmosphere and sound design this game offers. I wish there were more games that gave you the kind of vibrant chill setting that Night in the Woods presents. It's my favorite kind of atmosphere, and the experience of playing this wouldn't have been nearly the same had the graphics or sounds been different.
I would recommend this game to anyone who loves connecting deeply with characters, dark mysterious themes, philosophy, existentialism, story-over-action, and vibrant and melancholy atmospheres.
I wouldn't recommend this to impatient people or people that play games for action or don't care for THUROUGH interaction with the environment.

Is there really anything to say about this game that hasn't already been said? Probably not. Dark Souls (1) is the game that started an entire genre of RPG and combat mechanics. It gets a lot of praise for that and it's entirely deserved. It's a flawed masterpiece of a game. So much of this game combines into one experience that is constantly compelling. The open and connected world, the hints of Metroidvania level design, the tactical combat, the death mechanics, atmosphere and so on. There are tons of secrets to be found and yes, they'll require several playthroughs to find them all. There are many different ways to play and the game doesn't mind you changing half way through the game too much.
While the Dark Souls series sells itself as a game where you die and die again and lethal difficulty, it's more fair to say that this game is hard but fair. The game doesn't just screw you over without allowing you to learn and improve the entire time. And if you find the challenge to be too much, there are plenty of in-game ways to make things easier from summoning specters/friends to items that make combat easier. And they are all perfectly valid ways to play.
Things to keep in mind. Dark Souls 1 is the roughest entry in terms of the PC port. An Xbox or Steam controller is absolutely required to have an enjoyable experience. Trying to play this on a mouse + keyboard is going to be a miserable experience. It also runs at a locked 30FPS that can be unlocked to 60FPS but it's not without physics problems. There are entire levels that are performance problem hells which isn't fantastic. I feel that mods are required for the optimum experience for DS1. There are plenty of mods that correct a lot of the consolitis issues that ported over but they can't fix everything. This game was unfortunately rushed out to gauge interest in the series on PC and was only given minimal fixes afterwards.
So, I recommend finding and installing the mods and then enjoying. It's one hell of a memorable RPG. The world, characters and story all leave a mark on those that play. It's one of my more favored RPGs of all time. So good luck. Oh and don't forget to praise the sun.

Definitely one of the better Koei strategy games I have been playing so far (having played RTK from genesis to PC platform and Nobunaga series from series 10 till now).

I would like to start by saying I am a big fan of Koei. I have played many of the RotTK, Dynasty Warriors, Nobunaga's Ambition, and Samurai Warriors games. I wanted to like this game when I bought it.
I played through the tutorial where you are guided into selecting what to do on each turn. The city commands it was instructing me to do felt trivial: Press button->More rice | Press button->More soldiers. It felt very uninteresting and did not make me feel like I was preparing for the upcoming battle the tutorial was eluding to. Seeing all of the grayed out buttons I could not select did have me optimistic, though.
After too many turns of making more rice, I finally got to enter the battle. The battles in this game are like a real-time version of Dynasty Tactics, if you are familiar with this old title (also made by Koei). Troop-blob attacks troop-blob and there are officer commands that are usable that cause status effects for your troops or the enemy's. Again, what I was doing felt very trivial. As the battle went on I just sat there wondering, "Am I winning?"
After the tutorial, I started a new game. I chose a random daimyo to play as and got into it. The next hour was me pressing buttons to make more rice and make more troops. I increased my trust with a neighboring clan (This feature, btw, makes no sense - You simply gain trust then spend it as a currency, effectively making the AI do what you want). After the "build up", I attacked a nearby clan with the help of a tribe and my neighbor's forces I called in. We walked up to the city, stood around for minute, and won. Such fun. I am not doing this for hours/days/weeks. Escape->Quit Game
I understand that there may be more to the game than what I experienced. I looked around in all of the menus trying to find something interesting, or something I was missing, or not understanding. My imagination cannot even trick me into thinking there is more depth to this game than what I saw. It felt like I was playing a SNES game with simplistic mechanics but today's graphics. In all honesty, the SNES version of Nobunaga's Ambition is more fun than this. I guess my expectations were entirely too high for what I got.

I ignored the comparatively poor rating because this game reminded me of an updated version of one of my all-time favourites, Transport Tycoon. Unfortunately, reports of it being incomplete and buggy are actually pretty spot-on.
I played for a little over an hour, and in that time I had to restart multiple games, mainly because pathing became broken.
For example: Build a road between two resource points - set up a couple of cart-horses to transport goods from one to another via their respective stations. It all goes well for a while, and the money starts to flow.
Then I build another road, attaching to the existing road, to allow me to transport in a third resource.
Suddenly, my cart horses leap across the map, and are on the new road, ignoring their old route. I wait, thinking that they'll return once they get to the end. Nope. The horses disappear, and the carts just sit there, racking up maintenance bills until I run out of money again.
If this was a one-off, I would have been OK with it, and put it down to a glitch... but it seems I can't add any connections to roads which have 'routes' attached to them without something screwing up. This is pretty fundamental, and makes the game too awkward to play.
I loved the concept of this game, but the execution is incomplete. This is not a finished game.
